gaps.construction: Possessive article mein → meinen (Ich suche meinen Schlüssel)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "only the masculine forms change (der → den, ein → einen, kein → keinen, mein → meinen)"
gaps.note: The page's table and examples cover only der/ein/kein; mein/meinen (possessives) is never shown or said to follow the ein/kein pattern, yet an exercise could require meinen.

gaps.construction: Zero article for professions after werden/sein (Sie wird Ärztin)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [predicate-nominative-sein-werden-bleiben] ... (Er ist ein guter Lehrer; Sie wird Ärztin; Das bleibt kein Geheimnis)
gaps.note: The page never shows or explains that a profession as complement of werden/sein can take no article (Sie wird Ärztin), so a learner would not know how to handle this variant when an exercise asks for it.

gaps.construction: Adjective ending after ein in the nominative (ein guter Lehrer)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "the complement of sein/werden/bleiben also stays nominative (Er ist ein guter Lehrer — never accusative)"
gaps.note: The curriculum's model sentence has an adjective with the ending -er after ein, but the page only shows article + noun and never explains adjective endings, so a gap-fill on 'ein guter Lehrer' has no support.

gaps.construction: Dative personal pronouns (mir, dir, ihm, ihr, uns, euch, ihnen), e.g. "Ich helfe dir"
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Using accusative objects with dative verbs ("*Ich helfe dich" instead of "Ich helfe dir").
gaps.note: The page uses "dir" once in a pitfall but never gives the dative pronoun forms, so a learner could not fill in a pronoun after helfen, danken, gefallen or schmecken.

gaps.construction: Adjective ending after einen in the accusative (einen guten Bäcker)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: Es gibt hier einen guten Bäcker.
gaps.note: The page uses 'einen guten Bäcker' as an example but only explains the article einen. It never explains the accusative adjective ending -en, so an exercise that adds an adjective would not be covered.

gaps.construction: -er plural where the stem vowel allows no umlaut (das Kind → Kinder)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [plural-er-umlaut] a noun whose plural adds -er, with an umlaut where the vowel allows one (das Buch → Bücher, das Kind → Kinder)
gaps.note: The page presents -er only as 'with umlaut' and gives only umlauted examples, so a learner is not shown that -er stays umlaut-free when the stem vowel is e/i (Kind → Kinder).

gaps.construction: -en vs -n choice within the -(e)n class (die Frau → Frauen, die Lampe → Lampen)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [plural-en] a noun whose plural adds -(e)n, the default for feminines in -e (die Lampe → Lampen, die Frau → Frauen)
gaps.note: The page writes -(e)n and shows only -e feminines taking -n. It never explains when to add -en rather than -n, and it has no example like die Frau → Frauen.

gaps.construction: ihr- for a plural possessor (3pl), e.g. Die Kinder suchen ihren Ball.
gaps.curriculumEvidence: coverageSpec: person: 1sg, 2sg, 3sg, 1pl, 2pl, 3pl
gaps.note: The page only says a female possessor uses ihr- and glosses ihr as 'her/their' in the table. It never states that plural possessors also take ihr-, and it has no example, so a 3pl exercise would have no clear rule to follow.

gaps.construction: Other stem-changing verbs beyond sprechen/lesen/fahren (geben→gibt, helfen→hilft, sehen→siehst, empfehlen→empfiehlt, schlafen→schläft, tragen→trägt)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [stem-change-e-to-i] "sprechen→sprichst/spricht, geben→gibst/gibt, helfen→hilfst/hilft"; [stem-change-e-to-ie] "lesen→liest, sehen→siehst/sieht, empfehlen→empfiehlt"; [stem-change-a-to-ae] "schlafen→schläft, tragen→trägt"
gaps.note: The page shows each pattern with only one verb and never lists which common verbs follow which pattern, so an exercise on geben, helfen, sehen, empfehlen, schlafen or tragen asks the learner to pick a pattern the page doesn't tell them.

gaps.construction: vor + dative meaning 'ago' (vor einer Stunde)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [dative-relative-time] in / vor / nach + DATIVE for time relative to now or to another event (in zehn Minuten, vor einer Stunde, nach dem Essen)
gaps.note: The page only shows vor/nach with a reference event (vor dem Kurs, nach dem Abendessen) and never explains vor + time span relative to now ('ago', vor einer Stunde); an exercise would ask for this.

gaps.construction: um with half-hour clock times (um halb drei)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [um-clock-time] um + a clock time (um neun Uhr, um halb drei)
gaps.note: The page only shows um neun Uhr and um Mitternacht; it never explains the German 'halb + next hour' system an exercise on um halb drei would require.

gaps.construction: oder as a coordinating conjunction not occupying position 1 (Oder ich gehe ins Kino)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: a coordinating conjunction (und, aber, denn, oder) which does NOT count as position 1
gaps.note: The page lists only und, aber, denn; an exercise using 'oder' would not be covered, though the general rule would likely transfer.

gaps.construction: Manner adverb/adverbial phrase fronted (Leider gehe ich nicht ins Kino)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: an ADVERB or adverbial phrase (time, place, manner) occupies position 1
gaps.note: The page mentions only time and place adverbs for fronting, with no manner example; the rule would transfer but exercises might use manner adverbs.

gaps.construction: Fronted-adverb sentence where the page's only und/aber example does not show a clause opening with the conjunction (Und ich gehe ins Kino)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: the clause opens with a coordinating conjunction ... so subject-then-verb order follows it (Und ich gehe ins Kino)
gaps.note: The page states the rule, but its only example places 'aber' mid-sentence between two clauses, never showing a sentence-initial conjunction followed by subject-verb order or a conjunction followed by a fronted constituent.

gaps.construction: Adjective endings in the accusative after these prepositions (durch den kleinen Park, für einen guten Freund, ohne warme Jacke, bis nächsten Montag)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Article and adjective endings change accordingly
gaps.note: The page teaches only article and possessive changes. It never explains adjective endings (e.g. -en for masculine accusative, -e after die/das), so a learner could not fill in an adjective ending in an exercise. The phrases 'bis nächsten Montag' and 'die andere Mannschaft' appear without any explanation of their endings.

gaps.construction: Two-accusative verbs (Er fragt mich etwas; Sie lehrt ihn Deutsch; Das kostet mich einen Euro)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [two-accusative-verbs] a verb taking TWO accusative objects rather than a dative and an accusative (Das kostet mich einen Euro; Er fragt mich etwas; Sie lehrt ihn Deutsch)
gaps.note: The page raises kosten/fragen/lehren only in the pitfalls section, with one kosten example. It has no formation rule or examples for fragen or lehren, so an exercise that asks for a two-accusative sentence with those verbs gives the learner little to work from.

gaps.construction: Case forms of the stressed demonstrative pronoun (Den mag ich nicht. / Mit dem fahre ich nicht.)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: stressed der/das/die as demonstrative pronouns (Der ist gut!)
gaps.note: The page only shows nominative Der ist gut! and Das hier, and never says that the stressed pronoun takes the article's case forms (den, dem, der), so an exercise on accusative or dative pronoun use has no model.

gaps.construction: was für ein in the dative (Mit was für einem Auto fährst du?)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: coverageSpec: case: nominative, accusative, dative
gaps.note: The table and examples show only nominative and accusative forms. The page says ein declines normally, but it never shows a dative form such as einem or einer.

gaps.construction: derselbe full declension (dieselbe Frau, demselben Mann, derselben Frau)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: derselbe "the same" fuses article + selb- (denselben Fehler, im selben Haus)
gaps.note: The page gives only nominative masculine, accusative masculine and the contracted im selben. It has no feminine, neuter, plural or non-contracted dative forms (demselben, derselben), so such exercises would require forms the page does not show.

gaps.construction: alles/alle across cases (nominative/accusative: Alles ist gut; Ich kenne alle)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "alles/alle"; coverageSpec: case: nominative, accusative, dative
gaps.note: The page only shows the dative (mit allem, mit allen) and says they "decline", without giving nominative or accusative forms or example sentences, so an exercise on alles/alle in those cases has little to rely on.

gaps.construction: Reflexive causative with dative reflexive pronoun: Sie lässt sich die Haare schneiden / Ich lasse mir die Haare schneiden
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: causative lassen — ... (Lässt du dein Fahrrad reparieren?; Sie lässt sich die Haare schneiden)
gaps.note: The page only shows 'Ich lasse mir die Haare schneiden' in the pitfalls section without explaining the dative reflexive pronoun (mir/dir/sich/uns...) used when having something done to oneself, so a learner could not produce 'sich die Haare schneiden'.

gaps.construction: Lasst uns / Lassen Sie uns + infinitive (plural and formal suggestion forms)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: the imperative Lass uns / Lasst uns / Lassen Sie uns + infinitive, proposing a joint action
gaps.note: The page only teaches 'Lass uns …'; it never shows that the suggestion varies by addressee (ihr: Lasst uns …; formal: Lassen Sie uns …), which an exercise would demand.

gaps.construction: Question form / inversion with lassen (Lässt du dein Fahrrad reparieren?)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: causative lassen — ... (Lässt du dein Fahrrad reparieren?; ...)
gaps.note: No yes/no question example with lassen is shown, though the general rule and conjugation table make it largely derivable.

gaps.construction: Mixed verbs with stem change plus -t (bringen → gebracht, mitbringen → mitgebracht)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [infix-ge-separable-verbs] "a SEPARABLE-prefix verb, where ge- goes INSIDE between prefix and stem (eingekauft, aufgestanden, mitgebracht)"
gaps.note: The page only gives -t (unchanged stem) or -en (ablaut) patterns, so a learner can't work out mitgebracht, which has a stem change plus -t. An exercise using mitbringen would need this.

gaps.construction: ander- after the definite article (der andere Weg, die anderen Kinder)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "ander- declines like an adjective (der andere Weg, etwas anderes)."
gaps.note: The page only tabulates ander- after indefinite ein (mixed endings) and bare plural; an exercise on der/die/das + ander- (weak endings, e.g. der andere Weg, die anderen Kinder) is only covered by the vague phrase 'like a regular adjective'.

gaps.construction: Declined viele/wenige in non-nominative cases (mit vielen Freunden)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "decline in the plural (viele Freunde, wenige Fehler)"
gaps.note: The page says to add 'standard plural adjective endings' but only shows nominative/accusative forms, so a learner gets no worked example of the dative plural -en (vielen Freunden).

gaps.construction: einander and fused forms miteinander / voneinander (e.g. Sie helfen einander; Sie sprechen miteinander)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: formal einander (+ fused miteinander, voneinander), with gegenseitig as disambiguator
gaps.note: The page only names einander, miteinander and voneinander in passing and never shows a full sentence or explains how the preposition fuses with einander, so an exercise that asks for one of these forms gets little support.

gaps.construction: seit + Perfekt for a series of separate completed occurrences (Er ist seit Mai oft krank gewesen)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "the Perfekt is used ... for a series of separate occurrences (Er ist seit Mai oft krank gewesen)"; constructionVariants seit-perfekt-negated: "or a series of separate completed occurrences"
gaps.note: The page only covers the Perfekt for events that have not happened; it never explains that repeated, separate occurrences since a point in time also take the Perfekt, so a learner could not choose the tense for an exercise like 'Er ___ seit Mai oft krank ___'.

gaps.construction: darum / deswegen as synonyms of deshalb (Ich bin krank, darum bleibe ich zu Hause; ..., deswegen bleibe ich ...)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: deshalb (or darum/deswegen) introducing a CONSEQUENCE in a main clause, forcing verb-subject inversion
gaps.note: The page only teaches deshalb and never says that darum and deswegen work the same way and also trigger inversion, so an exercise using them would have no support.

gaps.construction: können + bare language name (Er kann Deutsch)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [koennen-for-skills] können + an infinitive (or a bare language name) for a MASTERED SKILL, where English "know how to" tempts wissen (Sie kann gut kochen; Er kann Deutsch)
gaps.note: The page says können is followed by an infinitive and never shows können with a language name and no infinitive, so a learner couldn't solve an exercise like "Er ___ Deutsch" (kann, not weiß or kennt).

gaps.construction: Dative forms of nominalized adjectives for people and plurals (dem Bekannten, einem Bekannten, einer Bekannten, mit den Deutschen, mit Bekannten)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: coverageSpec: case: nominative, accusative, dative
gaps.note: The formation table covers only nominative and accusative. Dative appears once, as 'mit etwas Neuem', so an exercise that asks for dative singular or plural forms of der/ein Bekannte has no table or explicit endings to rely on.

gaps.construction: Personal attribute nouns (non-body-part) with article instead of possessive, e.g. Sie schüttelte den Kopf / Er verlor die Geduld/die Stimme
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: a definite article standing in for a POSSESSIVE with a body part or personal attribute (Er hob die Hand; Sie schüttelte den Kopf)
gaps.note: The page names 'attributes' but every example is a body part, so an exercise using a personal attribute noun (e.g. voice, name) gets no illustration.

gaps.construction: Full declension endings across case/gender/number (acc., dat., fem./plural), e.g. mit besserer Qualität, für den besten Preis, in größeren Städten
gaps.curriculumEvidence: coverageSpec: number: singular, plural; case: nominative, accusative, dative
gaps.note: The page only shows nominative singular masculine in the formation table, plus one dative example (größerem). It gives no strong or weak ending paradigm for accusative, dative, feminine or plural, so a learner cannot work out endings for every case and number an exercise could ask for.

gaps.construction: Dative (and accusative) plural after quantifiers, e.g. mit allen guten Freunden vs. mit vielen guten Freunden / vielen guten Ideen
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "weak -en after alle, strong endings after viele/einige/mehrere/wenige" with coverageSpec case: nominative, accusative, dative
gaps.note: The quantifier table covers only plural nominative/accusative, and the only other-case example is genitive. Dative plural (allen guten Freunden, vielen guten Freunden, einigen guten Ideen) is only vaguely asserted ('the same logic holds'). The page never shows the quantifier's own ending or the strong dative -en on the adjective.

gaps.construction: Comparative/superlative after quantifiers, e.g. alle besten Freunde, viele bessere Angebote, einige größere Probleme
gaps.curriculumEvidence: name: "Attributive comparatives/superlatives + declension after quantifiers"
gaps.note: The page treats degree adjectives and quantifier declension separately and never shows a comparative or superlative combined with a quantifier, which an exercise could require.

gaps.construction: es fällt mir schwer / es geht mir um … (further fixed es + dative expressions)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants [es-tut-mir-leid-fixed]: "es tut mir leid, es fällt mir schwer, es geht mir um …"
gaps.note: The page only teaches es tut mir leid, so an exercise on es fällt mir schwer or es geht mir um … (es plus dative experiencer plus complement) has no model to work from.

gaps.construction: wie geht es dir? / Mir geht es gut (asking and reporting wellbeing)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants [es-geht-wellbeing]: "the wie geht es …? frame for asking or reporting how someone is (Wie geht es dir? — Mir geht es gut)"
gaps.note: Wie geht es dir? appears once in a list. The page never shows the dative person, other persons (Ihnen, ihm), or the reply Mir geht es gut, which an exercise would ask the learner to produce.

gaps.construction: placeholder es with zu-infinitive clause (Es ist wichtig, jeden Tag zu üben)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants [placeholder-es-clause]: "placeholder es holding the subject slot for a following dass-clause or zu-infinitive (… Es ist wichtig, jeden Tag zu üben)"
gaps.note: The page mentions "infinitive clause" once but gives no zu-infinitive example and no es + adjective/sein pattern (es ist wichtig). It also does not show fronting of a zu-infinitive clause.

gaps.construction: Present tense for timetable/booking-fixed events with a fixing cue (Der Zug fährt um 7:14 ab; Laut Stundenplan beginnt der Kurs nächste Woche; Die Ausstellung öffnet am Montag)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "the PRESENT tense for a future event that is FIXED BY A SCHEDULE, TIMETABLE OR BOOKING — not merely a plan or intention... carry an explicit cue such as \"laut Fahrplan\" / \"laut Stundenplan\" / \"planmäßig\""
gaps.note: The page only illustrates this with the plain-intention example "Morgen fahre ich nach Köln" and lumps 'planned' with 'on a schedule'; it never shows timetable/appointment/opening-time sentences or cues like laut Fahrplan/planmäßig, which the exercises will use to signal that the present is required.

gaps.construction: während + genitive (während des Unterrichts)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [genitive-preposition] a genitive PREPOSITION governing the phrase (trotz, wegen, innerhalb, außerhalb, während + genitive)
gaps.note: The page lists only trotz, wegen, innerhalb and außerhalb as genitive prepositions and never mentions während, which an exercise might use.

gaps.construction: Other fixed temporal genitives (eines Abends, eines Morgens)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [temporal-genitive-fixed] a fixed temporal genitive used adverbially (eines Tages, eines Abends)
gaps.note: The page shows only eines Tages and calls it frozen. It never shows that other time nouns work the same way (eines Abends), so an exercise on a different noun would be unsupported.

gaps.construction: Bare hin / her without a prepositional element (Komm her! / Geh hin!)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [hin-her-bare] BARE hin or her carrying the speaker-perspective on its own, with no prepositional element attached (Komm her!; Geh hin!)
gaps.note: The page says the words "rarely stand alone" and gives no example or rule for bare hin/her with a verb (Komm her! / Geh hin!), though exercises will test this variant.

gaps.construction: Plural subjects across the passive forms, e.g. Die Briefe wurden geschrieben / sind geschrieben worden / müssen geschrieben werden
gaps.curriculumEvidence: coverageSpec: number: singular, plural
gaps.note: The table and all examples use 3rd sg. subjects. Plural appears only as wurden/sind in the formulas, and the page never shows plural modal agreement (müssen/mussten). An exercise with a plural subject would rely on the learner inferring it.

gaps.construction: Past-tense progressive with war: Er war beim Aufräumen
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: beim-nominalized-infinitive: "(Ich bin beim Kochen; Er war beim Aufräumen)"
gaps.note: The page only shows sein in the present tense (bin/ist/sind), so it never shows that these constructions also work in the past (war/waren). An exercise using "Er war beim Aufräumen" or "Sie war dabei, ... zu packen" is not covered.

gaps.construction: setzen / sitzen (Ich setze das Kind auf den Stuhl — Das Kind sitzt auf dem Stuhl)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: transitive placement verbs take the accusative (stellen, legen, setzen, hängen, stecken ...), their stative partners take the dative (stehen, liegen, sitzen, hängen ...)
gaps.note: The page says it covers only three pairs and never mentions setzen or sitzen, so a learner could not handle an exercise that asks for setzen (acc.) versus sitzen (dat.).

gaps.construction: stecken as a placement verb (Ich stecke den Schlüssel in die Tasche)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: transitive placement verbs take the accusative (stellen, legen, setzen, hängen, stecken — Ich stelle die Vase auf den Tisch)
gaps.note: The page never mentions stecken, its meaning, or its use with in + accusative, so an exercise on it could not be solved from the page.

gaps.construction: damit + modal verb clause (…, damit wir pünktlich ankommen können)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [damit-modal-outcome] damit + a modal verb clause expressing an enabled outcome (…, damit wir pünktlich ankommen können)
gaps.note: The page only shows a modal in a damit clause inside a pitfall correction (…, damit meine Kinder dort studieren können). It never explains that the modal is the conjugated verb at the end, after the infinitive, or when to use a modal to express an enabled outcome, so an exercise on this variant has little to rely on.

gaps.construction: Bare infinitive after gehen/sehen/hören/lassen with example (Ich gehe schwimmen; Ich höre ihn kommen)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [bare-infinitive-no-zu] a BARE infinitive with NO zu, because the governing verb is a modal or gehen/sehen/hören/lassen (Ich muss arbeiten; Ich gehe schwimmen; Ich höre ihn kommen)
gaps.note: The page only lists gehen/sehen/hören/lassen in a note with no example of them (only modal example in pitfalls); an exercise with 'Ich höre ihn kommen' has no model.

gaps.construction: Optional dann after a wenn-clause (Wenn das Wetter schlecht ist, dann bleiben wir zu Hause)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [wenn-clause] a plain wenn-clause stating the condition, verb-final, optionally picked up by dann
gaps.note: The page mentions a resumptive dann only for the verb-first pattern and never shows it with a wenn-clause, so an exercise on wenn ... dann has no direct model.

gaps.construction: somit as a main-clause consecutive connector (Er kam zu spät; somit verpasste er den Zug)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [main-clause-connector-inversion] a MAIN-clause consecutive connector — folglich, infolgedessen, demzufolge, somit — taking V2 inversion
gaps.note: The page teaches folglich, infolgedessen and demzufolge with V2 inversion but never mentions somit, so an exercise that uses somit has no matching item on the page, although the general inversion rule would carry over.

gaps.construction: Obligatory vs. optional da(r)-correlate (Ich bin (daran) gewöhnt, früh aufzustehen; Angst davor, dass …)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Dropping the da(r)-correlate before a dass-clause where the noun/adjective requires it (with many adjectives it is optional: Ich bin (daran) gewöhnt, früh aufzustehen).
gaps.note: The page says the correlate is optional with many adjectives and omittable with stolz, but never says when it is obligatory (e.g. with nouns or certain adjectives). Its pitfalls only address the bare preposition, not dropping a required correlate, so an exercise on that error has no rule to rely on.

gaps.construction: irgendjemand in the dative (mit irgendjemandem) and irgendetwas/irgendwer case forms
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: irgend- compounds (irgendjemand, irgendwo/irgendwohin, irgendein-) ... coverageSpec: case: nominative, accusative, dative
gaps.note: The page gives only the accusative irgendjemanden in a parenthetical, and never gives the dative irgendjemandem, so a dative-case drill on irgendjemand would have to be guessed.

gaps.construction: möge in indirect requests (Sie bat, er möge sich melden)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [indirect-command-solle-moege] an indirect COMMAND or request rendered with solle or möge (Er sagte, wir sollten warten; Sie bat, er möge sich melden)
gaps.note: The page names möge in one clause, but every example uses solle. It never shows möge in a sentence, never says it is the Konjunktiv I of mögen, and never contrasts it with solle for requests. An exercise on 'er möge sich melden' would have no model.

gaps.construction: Forming the Konjunktiv II substitute forms (sie kämen, sie hätten, wir gingen)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [konjunktiv-ii-fallback] Konjunktiv II substituted BECAUSE the Konjunktiv I form would be identical to the indicative — typically the plural or 1sg (Sie sagten, sie kämen später — not *sie kommen)
gaps.note: The page explains when to substitute, but it only gives hätten and kämen as examples. It gives no rule for building Konjunktiv II (Präteritum stem, umlaut, endings), so a learner has no way to produce it for other verbs across 1sg, 1pl and 3pl.

gaps.construction: Verb-first / past-tense unreal wish: Wäre ich nur früher gekommen!
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [unreal-wish-exclamative] an unreal WISH or exclamative rather than a condition, typically with doch or nur (Wenn ich das doch wüsste!; Wäre ich nur früher gekommen!)
gaps.note: The page only shows a present wish as a stand-alone wenn-clause with doch. It never shows a wenn-less verb-first wish with nur, or a past wish with Konjunktiv II perfect. An exercise on Wäre ich nur früher gekommen! would have to combine other sections.

gaps.construction: Bare als + verb-first unreal comparison (Er tut so, als hätte er nichts gewusst / als wüsste er nichts)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [als-ob-unreal-comparison] an unreal COMPARISON with als ob (or bare als + verb-first) plus Konjunktiv II
gaps.note: The page mentions in passing that als takes verb-second order. It gives no example and no explanation of the bare als construction, so an exercise asking for als + inverted verb would have little support.

gaps.construction: Constituent negation with sondern contrast (Er kommt nicht heute, sondern morgen)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: nicht-placement — "immediately before the constituent it negates ... Er kommt nicht heute, sondern morgen"
gaps.note: The page states the rule that nicht goes directly before the negated element, but it gives no worked example of constituent negation, and it never shows the sondern contrast. An exercise asking the learner to place nicht before a focused adverbial and add sondern would get little help from the page.

gaps.construction: bloß/nur in wish clauses (Wenn er nur bald käme!)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [bloss-nur-urgency-warning] bloß or nur adding URGENCY to a warning, wish or command (Mach das bloß nicht!; Wenn er nur bald käme!)
gaps.note: The page says bloß intensifies longing in wishes and lists 'wish' in the table, but it gives no wish example and doesn't show the wenn-clause with Konjunktiv II and nur/bloß, so a learner can't build or recognise 'Wenn er nur bald käme!'.

gaps.construction: Funktionsverbgefüge with passive meaning (Anwendung finden = angewendet werden)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: formal Funktionsverbgefüge with passive meaning (Anwendung finden = angewendet werden)
gaps.note: The page never mentions Funktionsverbgefüge such as Anwendung finden, in Betracht gezogen werden or zur Anwendung kommen as passive equivalents, so an exercise asking for a paraphrase would have nothing to draw on.

gaps.construction: kriegen-passive (Er kriegt das Buch geschenkt)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [bekommen-passive] the bekommen/kriegen-passive, which promotes the DATIVE recipient to subject
gaps.note: The page covers only bekommen as the auxiliary and never says that kriegen (colloquial) works the same way.

gaps.construction: derjenige/diejenigen declension (e.g. denjenigen, demjenigen, derjenigen)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [derjenige-der] the heavy demonstrative antecedent derjenige/diejenigen followed by a der-relative (Diejenigen, die in den hinteren Reihen saßen, konnten nichts sehen)
gaps.note: The page only says derjenige is declined like a definite article plus adjective and gives one nominative-plural example. It has no paradigm and no example in an oblique case, so an exercise that needs denjenigen, demjenigen or derjenigen has little to work from.

gaps.construction: epistemic kann (Er kann sich geirrt haben)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [koennte-kann-epistemic] könnte or kann expressing epistemic POSSIBILITY, weaker than dürfte (Das könnte stimmen; Er kann sich geirrt haben)
gaps.note: The page names kann beside könnte in the meaning list but gives no example or table row for kann (present or perfect infinitive). An exercise using kann, as in 'Er kann sich geirrt haben', would have no model to follow.

gaps.construction: über-/unter- as variable prefixes (separable vs. inseparable), e.g. übersetzen (ferry across) vs. übersetzen (translate); unterstellen
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [variable-prefix-separable-literal] a VARIABLE prefix (um-, durch-, über-, unter-) used SEPARABLY (stressed prefix, with its own adverbial sense: turning over, through, over, under)
gaps.note: The page only works through um- and durch- (umfahren, durchschauen) and never shows über- or unter- verbs or states their separable senses (over, under), so an über-/unter- exercise would rely on generalising from um-/durch-.

gaps.construction: gustar-type verbs with plural subject (Nos encantan los deportes)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [gustar-definite-article] the definite article before the subject of gustar or a verb like it — encantar, molestar, interesar (Me gusta la música clásica; Nos encantan los deportes)
gaps.note: The page only says 'gustar and similar verbs' and shows singular me gusta; it never names encantar/molestar/interesar or shows plural agreement (gustan/encantan + los/las + plural noun), which plural-number exercises would require.

gaps.construction: hay + bare plural noun (Hay sillas libres en la sala)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [hay-no-article] impersonal hay followed by a noun with NO article at all (Hay leche en la nevera; Hay sillas libres en la sala)
gaps.note: The page only shows singular examples (hay leche, hay un café) and never shows a plural noun with no article after hay, which a plural-number exercise would test.

gaps.construction: Single ni after the first item (No como carne ni pescado)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: No como carne ni pescado.
gaps.note: The page only teaches the doubled pattern «no … ni X ni Y». It never says that the first ni can be dropped after a negative verb, so a learner couldn't work out an exercise that uses the curriculum's own form «no como carne ni pescado».

gaps.construction: Place adverbs aquí / ahí / allí (Aquí construiremos la casa, ahí el garaje y allí la piscina)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: The place adverbs aquí/ahí/allí mirror the same three distances.
gaps.note: The page never mentions aquí/ahí/allí, their meanings, or their correspondence to este/ese/aquel, yet a constructionVariant requires sentences contrasting at least two of them.

gaps.construction: Gendered demonstrative pronoun standing alone (¿Te gusta esta camisa? Prefiero aquella)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [demonstrative-pronoun-gendered] a GENDERED demonstrative pronoun standing alone in place of a noun already understood, with no noun after it
gaps.note: The page says demonstratives can be pronouns and shows only 'Este es mi profesor'; it never explains dropping a noun with a contrastive choice (e.g., Prefiero aquella) or how the pronoun agrees with the omitted noun.

gaps.construction: Invariable compound/noun-derived colour adjectives (camisa verde oscuro, botones naranja, calcetines rojo claro)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [invariable-compound-colour-adjectives, share 2] a colour adjective that never agrees — a noun-derived colour (naranja, rosa, violeta) or a compound (verde oscuro, azul claro)
gaps.note: The page never mentions colour adjectives that stay unchanged (naranja, rosa, verde oscuro), so a learner could not do an exercise like 'tres botones ___ (naranja)' or 'hojas verde oscuro'.

gaps.construction: Fully invariable adjectives (estándar, gratis, macho, hembra): los coches estándar, las entradas gratis
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: A few adjectives are invariable for both gender and number (estándar, gratis: los coches estándar, las entradas gratis).
gaps.note: The page teaches only gender-invariable adjectives that still pluralize, and never mentions adjectives that stay the same in the plural, so exercises on estándar/gratis cannot be solved.

gaps.construction: Pluralizing noun-derived or compound colour adjectives error (*tres botones naranjas, *hojas verdes oscuras)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Pluralizing noun-derived or compound colour adjectives ("*tres botones naranjas", "*hojas verdes oscuras" instead of "tres botones naranja", "hojas verde oscuro").
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address this error, and the page never teaches the rule that avoids it.

gaps.construction: Collective noun takes singular agreement (la gente es amable)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Giving a collective noun plural agreement ("*la gente son amables" instead of "la gente es amable").
gaps.note: The page never mentions that collective nouns like gente take singular verb and adjective agreement.

gaps.construction: Plural formation of regular adjectives and default agreement (rojo/roja/rojos/rojas, nuevo/nueva)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [descriptive-adjective-agreement-default, share 3] a plain descriptive adjective agreeing ... (un coche rojo, una casa roja, unos zapatos negros, unas sillas nuevas)
gaps.note: The page shows only the gentilicio table and never states the basic -o/-a pattern and plural -s/-es rules for ordinary adjectives like rojo/negro/nuevo.

gaps.construction: Invariable gentilicios ending in -e such as belga, estadounidense (una amiga belga)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: a gentilicio ending in -í or -e that does NOT add -a (marroquí, iraní, israelí, belga, estadounidense)
gaps.note: The page names belga and canadiense only in passing in the intro and its rule covers just -í, not -e endings, so exercises on belga/estadounidense have thin support.

gaps.construction: hay with a bare mass noun (Hay leche en la nevera)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [hay-bare-noun-or-number] invariable hay with NO article — a bare mass noun or a numeral, never pluralized (Hay leche en la nevera; Hay dos bancos aquí)
gaps.note: The page only says 'or no article at all' in a bullet and never shows a bare or mass-noun example, so an exercise like 'Hay leche/agua/ruido…' has no model.

gaps.construction: hay with abstract nouns (Hay un problema con la reserva; Hay ruido; Hay un accidente)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [hay-abstract-noun] hay with an abstract, non-locatable noun such as problema, ruido or accidente, where estar is impossible (Hay un problema con la reserva)
gaps.note: The rule appears only in a parenthetical, with no example of hay plus an abstract noun and no explanation of why estar is impossible, though an exercise could demand choosing hay for such nouns.

gaps.construction: estar with an indefinite, numeral-quantified person (Dos policías están en la puerta esperándote)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [estar-indefinite-locatable] estar with an indefinite but movable person or thing whose existence is taken for granted (Dos policías están en la puerta esperándote)
gaps.note: The page gives one singular example (Un señor está en la puerta) and says numbers mean hay, so it never shows that an indefinite plural or numeral-quantified person can take estar when existence is assumed.

gaps.construction: Bare locative adverbs without de — fuera, dentro, arriba, abajo (Vamos a cenar fuera esta noche; Te espero abajo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [bare-adverbs-no-de] a bare locative adverb that takes NO de at all — fuera, dentro, arriba, abajo (Vamos a cenar fuera esta noche; Te espero abajo)
gaps.note: The page teaches only fuera de/dentro de with a noun and never says these can stand alone as adverbs without de, nor mentions arriba/abajo; an exercise would require choosing the bare adverb.

gaps.construction: Motion-direction adverbs adentro/afuera, adelante, atrás (Sigue adelante y no mires hacia atrás; Dio un paso atrás)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [motion-adverbs-adentro-afuera-adelante-atras] a motion-direction adverb where the static form would be wrong — adentro/afuera, adelante, atrás
gaps.note: The page covers only static location and never presents adentro/afuera, adelante, atrás or contrasts them with static detrás/delante, so a learner couldn't solve such exercises.

gaps.construction: entre meaning 'among' a group (Entre mis amigos, nadie fuma)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [entre-among] entre meaning 'among' within a group rather than between two points (Entre mis amigos, nadie fuma)
gaps.note: The page presents entre only as 'between ... y ...'; the 'among' sense with a single group noun phrase is never taught.

gaps.construction: Error: using static detrás/delante where motion needs atrás/adelante (*dar un paso detrás)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Using static detrás/delante where motion needs atrás/adelante ("*dar un paso detrás" instead of "dar un paso atrás").
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address this static vs. motion error.

gaps.construction: Compound locative after another preposition (El perro salió de detrás del coche)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [de-el-contraction-del] ... (La farmacia está al lado del supermercado; El perro salió de detrás del coche)
gaps.note: The page never shows a locative preceded by another preposition (de detrás del coche); the del rule is covered generally, though.

gaps.construction: Confirmation tag ¿no? (Usted habla inglés, ¿no?; Vienes mañana, ¿no?)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: The tag ¿no? seeks confirmation (Usted habla inglés, ¿no?)
gaps.note: The page never mentions the tag ¿no? used to seek confirmation, so a learner could not complete or produce a statement closed with ¿no?.

gaps.construction: ya no 'no longer' (Ya no vivo aquí; Ya no fuma)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [ya-no-no-longer] ya no for 'no longer' — something that used to be true and has stopped (Ya no vivo aquí; Ya no fuma)
gaps.note: The page never teaches ya no meaning 'no longer', yet exercises will ask for it (e.g. Ya no vivimos aquí).

gaps.construction: Short answers with a following short clause / elliptical negative answer (¿Vienes? — No, hoy no; ¿Hablas español? — Sí, un poco)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [si-no-short-answers] optionally followed by a short clause (¿Hablas español? — Sí, un poco; ¿Vienes? — No, hoy no)
gaps.note: The page only shows Sí/No followed by a repeated verb, not bare Sí/No or answers with a short non-verbal clause like 'un poco' or 'hoy no'.

gaps.construction: Answering a negative question (¿No tienes coche? — No, no tengo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Answering a negative question with just "no" and dropping the second no ... answering "¿no tienes coche?" with "No, tengo"
gaps.note: The page's pitfall uses an affirmative question (¿Tienes coche?) and never addresses answering a negative question such as ¿No tienes coche?.

gaps.construction: también/tampoco with emphatic a mí + pronoun and subject pronoun (A mí también me gusta; Yo tampoco lo sabía; Yo también)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [tampoco-agreement-negative] (No me gusta el café. — A mí tampoco; Yo tampoco lo sabía)
gaps.note: The page shows only 'a Marta' and 'mi hermano' as subjects, never the 'a mí también/tampoco' or 'yo también' stand-alone replies, nor tampoco before an object pronoun plus verb.

gaps.construction: Profession -o → -a feminisation (el arquitecto / la arquitecta, el enfermero / la enfermera)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Profession nouns in -o form the feminine in -a (la arquitecta)
gaps.note: The page never says that profession nouns in -o change to -a for the feminine, so an exercise asking for la arquitecta or la enfermera has nothing to rely on.

gaps.construction: Invariable profession/role nouns (el/la juez, el/la estudiante, el/la periodista)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: some stay invariable, with the article marking sex (el/la juez)
gaps.note: The page does not explain that some nouns keep one form and only the article marks sex, so exercises on el/la juez, estudiante or periodista cannot be solved.

gaps.construction: Gender of countries (la España de hoy; todo México)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Countries in unstressed -a are feminine (la España de hoy); others are masculine (todo México).
gaps.note: The page says nothing about country names, so the rule that countries in unstressed -a are feminine and others masculine is not available for exercises.

gaps.construction: Gender-changing nouns with different meanings (el capital / la capital)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: El capital de la empresa está en la capital del país.
gaps.note: The page does not mention nouns whose meaning changes with gender, so an exercise on el capital vs. la capital cannot be solved.

gaps.construction: Invariable-gender noun agreeing with the grammatical gender, not the referent's sex (una persona simpática, la víctima)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Matching an invariable-gender noun to the referent's sex ("*un persona simpático" for a man instead of "una persona simpática"; la víctima can be a man).
gaps.note: The page says gender is not biological sex, but it never covers nouns like persona or víctima that keep one gender whatever the referent's sex, and the pitfalls section skips this error.

gaps.construction: Masculine plural for mixed-sex groups (mis hermanos, los padres)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Using the feminine plural for a mixed-sex group, missing that "mis hermanos" covers brothers and sisters and "los padres" means parents.
gaps.note: The page never explains that the masculine plural covers mixed groups, and the pitfalls section does not address this error.

gaps.construction: Other masculine -a/-ma and feminine -o exceptions (el mapa, la moto)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: a masculine noun in -a (el problema, el día, el mapa) or a feminine noun in -o (la mano, la foto, la moto)
gaps.note: The page gives the Greek -ma rule and covers problema, día, mano and foto, but el mapa and la moto are not shown. A learner would have to memorise them without the page's help.

gaps.construction: Gender of nouns in -e/consonant used in agreement; heteronyms el yerno / la nuera
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: a heteronym pair ... (el padre / la madre, el hombre / la mujer, el yerno / la nuera)
gaps.note: The page explains heteronyms with only two pairs. That is enough to generalise from, but it does not show further pairs such as el yerno / la nuera.

gaps.construction: Words in -o/-a taking article el with other items, e.g. el paraguas, el sacacorchos (compound nouns invariable, masculine)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: Dejé el paraguas junto al sacacorchos.
gaps.note: Compound nouns ending in -s (paraguas, sacacorchos) are masculine, but the page does not cover them. They could appear in an exercise as nouns ending in a consonant.

gaps.construction: Numbers as masculine nouns (un siete)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: Saqué un siete en el examen.
gaps.note: The page does not mention that a number used as a noun is masculine, though one example shows it.

gaps.construction: Attribute de for price, age, measurement (un coche de diez mil euros; un hombre de cuarenta años; una mesa de dos metros)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [de-attribute-price-age-measurement, share 2] attribute de giving a price, an age or a measurement
gaps.note: The page never mentions de with price, age or measurement, so a learner cannot produce items like 'un hombre de cuarenta años' or 'tres metros de largo'.

gaps.construction: con for contents (una cesta con pan, un vaso con agua)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: con describing a permanent feature or contents (una casa con jardín, una cesta con pan)
gaps.note: The page presents con only as a feature the noun has; the contents use (una cesta con pan, un vaso con agua) is not explained, though un café con leche hints at it.

gaps.construction: Avoiding a locative preposition between two nouns (*el libro en la mesa vs. el libro que está en la mesa / la casa de la colina)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Joining two nouns with a locative preposition on the English model ("*el libro en la mesa" instead of "el libro que está en la mesa" or "la casa de la colina").
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address using en to link two nouns or the alternatives with que está or de.

gaps.construction: Adjective placement after a de-compound (un lápiz de memoria barato, not *un lápiz barato de memoria)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Breaking up a de-compound with an adjective ("*un lápiz barato de memoria" instead of "un lápiz de memoria barato").
gaps.note: The page never says that an adjective follows the whole de-compound and must not interrupt it.

gaps.construction: Written accent loss in stressed -és/-ús plurals (inglés → ingleses, autobús → autobuses)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: plural-es-stressed-final-s: "taking -es and losing its written accent (país → países, inglés → ingleses, autobús → autobuses)"
gaps.note: The page only shows país → países and never says that the written accent is dropped in words like inglés and autobús, so a learner cannot spell ingleses or autobuses.

gaps.construction: Foreign loanwords add just -s (los anoraks)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "Foreign loanwords usually add just -s (los anoraks)"
gaps.note: Rule 2 says consonant-final nouns take -es, and the page never mentions that loanwords like anorak usually take only -s.

gaps.construction: Family surnames are invariable (los Pérez)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "family surnames are invariable (los Pérez)"
gaps.note: The page does not mention surnames, so an exercise asking for the plural of a family name could not be solved.

gaps.construction: Noun+noun compounds pluralize only the first noun (los años luz)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "in noun+noun compounds only the first noun pluralizes (los años luz)"
gaps.note: The page gives no rule for compound nouns, and an exercise would ask for the plural of a compound such as año luz.

gaps.construction: Stress-shifting plurals (carácter → caracteres, régimen → regímenes, espécimen → especímenes)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Keeping the singular stress in the three stress-shifting plurals (\"*los carácteres\" instead of \"los caracteres\"; el régimen → los regímenes, el espécimen → los especímenes)."
gaps.note: The pitfalls section never mentions these three nouns, whose stress moves in the plural.

gaps.construction: Millón/millones + de (dos millones de turistas; un millón doscientos mil euros)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Dropping de after millón/millones, e.g. "*dos millones turistas" instead of "dos millones de turistas"
gaps.note: The page never mentions millón/millones or the rule that de follows them before a noun (but not before further number words), which an exercise would test.

gaps.construction: Ordinal/cardinal word order with nouns (los tres primeros párrafos, not *los primeros tres párrafos)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Copying the English cardinal-ordinal order, e.g. "*los primeros tres párrafos" instead of "los tres primeros párrafos"
gaps.note: The page does not say that the cardinal precedes the ordinal when both modify a noun, so a learner cannot correct such an item.

gaps.construction: Article with numbered nouns (el piso 38, la página 5)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Nouns identified by a number take the article (el piso 38, la página 5).
gaps.note: The page never explains that nouns identified by a number take the definite article.

gaps.construction: Dates with cardinals (el veinticinco de febrero)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: Salimos el veinticinco de febrero.
gaps.note: The page gives no date pattern (el + cardinal + de + month), nor does it mention that el primero is the ordinal exception, apart from a brief 'el primero de mayo' aside.

gaps.construction: Cardinals 0–100 formation (quince, veinticinco, cuarenta; compound numbers like treinta y uno)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Cardinal numbers, including gender agreement of uno and -cientos ... Mi hermano tiene quince años.
gaps.note: The page has no table of basic cardinals (0–100) or rules for forming 16–29 as one word and 31+ with 'y'; exercises with quince or cuarenta would rely on this.

gaps.construction: Percentages and quantity nouns (el cuarenta por ciento; una docena de huevos)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: El cuarenta por ciento de los alumnos estudia inglés. / Compré una docena de huevos.
gaps.note: The page never teaches 'por ciento' or collective numerals like docena + de.

gaps.construction: cien vs. ciento and 'cientos' compounds (ciento veinte; cien before nouns)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: gender agreement of uno and -cientos with the counted noun
gaps.note: The page lists cien only in passing and shows no 100/101–199 forms or the cien/ciento distinction, and omits 400 and 600 forms.

gaps.construction: Cardinals above décimo replacing ordinals in uses like el siglo veinte
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Above décimo, everyday usage prefers cardinals (el siglo veinte).
gaps.note: The page gives only the example el piso once, with no explanation of cardinals placed after the noun for centuries, etc.

gaps.construction: Compound numbers with uno before nouns (treinta y un libros / una mesa; un/una agreement before feminine)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: gender agreement of uno ... (veintiún libros)
gaps.note: The page shows only 21 in the table, and does not generalize to 31, 41, 101 or to hundreds + uno (doscientas una mesas).

gaps.construction: Repeating the possessive before each of two referents (Llevaba mi chaqueta y mi corbata; Trajo su pasaporte y su billete), vs. one possessive for a single referent (mi amigo y compañero)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [repeated-possessive-two-referents] the possessive REPEATED before each of two distinct things, where English uses it once (Llevaba mi chaqueta y mi corbata...)
gaps.note: The page never says the possessive must be repeated before each noun when two different things are possessed (and not repeated for one referent), nor does it warn against *mi chaqueta y corbata; an exercise would require this.

gaps.construction: Fixed phrases with static 'a': a la vuelta, sentado a la mesa (plus a la derecha)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "apart from a few fixed phrases with a (a la derecha, a la vuelta, sentado a la mesa)"
gaps.note: The page only mentions estar a la derecha/a la izquierda/al lado de in a pitfalls parenthesis. It never shows or explains a la vuelta or sentado a la mesa, and it gives no framing of these as a set of exceptions, so an exercise on them would have no support.

gaps.construction: Present for imminent / just-arranged events (Me caso el sábado; ¡Ya voy!; Mañana abrimos a las nueve)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [present-for-imminent-arranged-events, share 3] the present for an imminent or already-arranged event, where English would use a future or a continuous (Me caso el sábado; Mañana abrimos a las nueve; ¡Ya voy!)
gaps.note: The page only covers fixed scheduled events (El tren sale a las ocho); it never teaches the imminent or just-arranged use (¡Ya voy!, Me caso el sábado) or that English future/continuous maps to the Spanish present.

gaps.construction: Present in offers and permission questions (¿Escribo yo a los abuelos?; ¿Abrimos la ventana?; ¿Nos vamos?)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [present-for-offers-permission, share 2] the present in a QUESTION that offers or asks permission (¿Escribo yo a los abuelos?; ¿Abrimos la ventana?)
gaps.note: The page has no mention of using the present to offer something or ask permission; the only question example (¿Hablas español?) is a plain yes/no question, so an exercise on offers would have no support.

gaps.construction: Avoiding the continuous for arranged events (*me estoy casando vs. me caso)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Using the continuous for an imminent arranged event by English transfer ("*me estoy casando" to announce a wedding plan instead of "me caso").
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address the English-transfer error of using estar + gerund for arranged future events.

gaps.construction: valer → valgo
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "-go forms hago, pongo, salgo, tengo, vengo, digo, oigo, traigo, valgo"
gaps.note: The page's -go list and table omit valer, so an exercise asking for valgo has no model on the page.

gaps.construction: Consonant + -cer verbs take -zo, not -zco (vencer → venzo, cocer → cuezo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "-zco forms of most vowel + -cer/-cir verbs (conozco, agradezco, conduzco; but venzo, cuezo)"
gaps.note: The page only says -zco follows a vowel. It never shows the consonant + -cer exceptions or the c→z spelling change (venzo, cuezo), so a learner could not produce those forms.

gaps.construction: Impersonal es + masculine adjective + infinitive (Es absurdo hacerlo así)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "masculine singular agreement for adjectives referring to an infinitive, a clause, or no specific noun (viajar es caro, es absurdo hacerlo)"
gaps.note: The page only shows the infinitive in subject-first position (Viajar es caro) and never shows or explains the Es + adjective + infinitive order or the impersonal 'no specific noun' use, which an exercise would require.

gaps.construction: Clause as subject and masculine singular adjective regardless of sentence topic
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "an infinitive (or a clause) as the subject, with the predicate adjective in the masculine singular regardless of what the sentence is about"
gaps.note: The page says the infinitive is treated as a masculine singular noun but never mentions a clause as subject or states that the adjective stays masculine singular (not agreeing with other nouns in the sentence), as in 'Viajar solo es caro'.

gaps.construction: ser de + material (La mesa es de madera)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: material with de (la mesa es de madera)
gaps.note: The page never mentions ser de + material (nor the example La mesa es de madera), so an exercise on what something is made of has no support.

gaps.construction: estar + temporary-state adjectives contrasted with ser + inherent adjectives (Mi hermana es muy simpática vs. Está cansada)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: ser + adjectives of inherent nature vs. estar + adjectives of temporary state
gaps.note: The page gives one inherent-adjective example (El hielo es frío) and only enfermo/bien/mal for estar, so it gives little help choosing between ser and estar with a range of adjectives such as simpática, difícil, cansado or contento.

gaps.construction: Pronoun with apposition/compound subject (Nosotros los estudiantes trabajamos mucho; Tú y yo vamos juntos al cine)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: Nosotros los estudiantes trabajamos mucho. / Tú y yo vamos juntos al cine.
gaps.note: The page never shows a pronoun combined with a noun phrase or a compound subject like 'tú y yo', so an exercise on these would have no model to follow.

gaps.construction: Pronoun after ser beyond 'soy yo' (Fueron ellas las que llamaron)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [pronoun-after-ser] the pronoun retained after ser, where Spanish keeps it (¿Quién es? — Soy yo; Fueron ellas las que llamaron)
gaps.note: The page gives only the single example 'Soy yo' and never shows other persons or the cleft 'ser + pronoun + las que' pattern.

gaps.construction: Not using él/ella for things (*él sopla → sopla; sin él is fine)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Using él/ella as a subject pronoun for a thing by analogy with English "it" ("*él sopla" for the wind instead of just "sopla")
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not say that Spanish has no subject pronoun for 'it' and that él/ella are not used for things as subjects.

gaps.construction: Definite article with days of the week (el lunes / los lunes)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [definite-article-days-of-week] the definite article with a day of the week: el lunes for one occasion, los lunes for a habit (El lunes tengo cita; Los lunes voy al gimnasio)
gaps.note: The page never mentions days of the week, el lunes vs. los lunes, or the errors '*en lunes' / '*voy lunes' / '*dos veces a semana'; an exercise would demand choosing el/los with days.

gaps.construction: Definite article with body parts (Me duele la cabeza; Levantó la mano)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [definite-article-clothing-possessions] the definite article — not a possessive — with clothing or body parts in an action (Se puso el abrigo; Me duele la cabeza; Levantó la mano)
gaps.note: The page only covers clothing/belongings with reflexive dressing; body parts (me duele la cabeza, levantó la mano) are never taught.

gaps.construction: Definite article with titles outside direct address (la señora Ruiz)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: titles outside direct address (la señora Ruiz)
gaps.note: Page never explains using the article before titles when talking about someone, versus omitting it in direct address (Buenos días, señora Ruiz).

gaps.construction: Definite article with places like en el hospital
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: definite article for ... places like en el hospital
gaps.note: The page does not mention article use with institutional places (en el hospital, en la escuela) so a learner could not do such items.

gaps.construction: Languages: no article after hablar/en, but article in el español de Chile
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: none with ... languages after hablar/en (hablo español — but el español de Chile)
gaps.note: The page never covers languages, so the zero article after hablar/en and the article when qualified or as subject are untaught.

gaps.construction: Unindefinite una/un with qualified profession for other professions; ser + 'Mi padre es ingeniero' role nouns
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [zero-article-unqualified-profession] NO article after ser with an unqualified profession or role (Es profesora; Mi padre es ingeniero)
gaps.note: Page covers professions but not 'role' nouns (non-job roles) explicitly; this is covered only through the profession rule.

gaps.construction: Zero article with unspecified plural nouns in existential/purchase contexts (Compramos naranjas; Hay niños en el parque)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [zero-article-mass-plural-unspecified] NO article with an unspecified mass or plural noun (Bebe agua; Compramos naranjas; Hay niños en el parque)
gaps.note: Plural rule appears only in a table row (Come verduras), with no explicit example with hay or comprar.

gaps.construction: Article omission after 'dos veces a la semana' (a la semana, with article for frequency)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: dropping the article altogether ("*voy lunes", "*dos veces a semana" instead of "dos veces a la semana")
gaps.note: The pitfalls section never addresses the article in 'a la semana' frequency expressions.

gaps.construction: Agreeing propio/propia: mi propio coche, el propio autor, con mis propios ojos
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: agreeing propio for own/self-same (mi propio coche, el propio autor)
gaps.note: The page never mentions propio; an exercise on 'Lo vi con mis propios ojos' or 'Lo dijo el propio autor' (agreement, position after possessive/article) cannot be solved from the page.

gaps.construction: Distributive de N en N: Los niños entraban de dos en dos; Subía los escalones de tres en tres
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [de-dos-en-dos] the distributive pattern de N en N describing how people or things move or are arranged (Los niños entraban de dos en dos)
gaps.note: The page has no mention of the de dos en dos pattern, so drills requiring de N en N have no support.

gaps.construction: cada uno de + plural: cada uno de mis amigos
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: cada día, cada dos semanas, cada uno de mis amigos
gaps.note: The pronominal use of cada uno de + plural possessive/noun is never shown, though the description lists it.

gaps.construction: Emphatic mismo agreeing in plural (nosotros mismos, ellas mismas) and emphatic mismo with noun
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [mismo-emphatic] emphatic mismo/misma right after a subject pronoun or noun
gaps.note: Only singular emphatic forms are shown in the table; plural emphatic forms are not shown, though agreement is stated generally.

gaps.construction: más/menos + NOUN + que (Tengo más libros que tú; Hoy hay menos gente que ayer)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: comparative-superiority: "más + adjective/adverb/noun + que"; comparative-inferiority: "menos + adjective/adverb/noun + que"
gaps.note: The formation table shows más/menos only with adjectives, adverbs and verbs. It never shows them directly before a noun, so a learner has no model for an exercise like 'Tengo ___ libros ___ tú'.

gaps.construction: luego vs. entonces temporal contrast (Primero cenamos y luego vimos una película; Entonces yo vivía en Sevilla)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "luego \"afterwards/later on\" vs. entonces \"then/at that moment\" (both can mean \"in that case\")"
gaps.note: The page never mentions luego or entonces as a temporal marker ('at that moment'), nor contrasts it with luego 'afterwards'; an exercise choosing between luego and entonces by time context could not be solved.

gaps.construction: Assertive «sí que» vs. rejoinder «pero si» (—No vendrá. —¡Sí que vendrá!; ¡Pero si te oí!)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "assertive sí que (¡Sí que vendrá!) vs. rejoinder pero si (¡Pero si te oí!)"
gaps.note: The page treats sí/si only as «yes/himself» vs. «if» and never shows emphatic «sí que» (accented) or the rejoinder «pero si» (unaccented), so an exercise on these would have no support.

gaps.construction: Adjective «solo/sola» (agreeing) vs. invariable adverb «solo» (Octavia volvió sola y solo quería descansar)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "solo as an ADJECTIVE agreeing with its subject (volvió sola) against solo as the invariable adverb 'only' — the contrast is the agreement, not the optional accent"
gaps.note: The page only notes in a side remark that adverb solo needs no accent and adjective solo never does; it never explains that the adjective agrees in gender/number (sola, solos) while the adverb stays invariable, nor gives a contrasting example sentence.

gaps.construction: Usted/ustedes take lo/la/los/las (Doctora, la llamé ayer = I called you)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "Usted/ustedes take these third-person forms (Doctora, la llamé ayer = I called you)."
gaps.note: The page never says that formal 'you' (usted/ustedes) is replaced by third-person lo/la/los/las, so a learner could not solve an exercise like 'Doctora, la llamé ayer'.

gaps.construction: Negative imperatives take proclisis (No lo compres)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "Negative imperatives take proclisis instead (No lo compres)"
gaps.note: The page only covers affirmative imperative enclisis and never says that negative commands put the pronoun before the verb.

gaps.construction: Written accent on enclitic forms (leyéndolo, cómpralo, llámala; buscándolas)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "with the written accent that keeps the stress (Estoy leyéndolo; Sigue buscándolas)"
gaps.note: Accented examples appear, but the page never explains when the written accent is needed after attaching a pronoun, which exercises on gerunds and imperatives would require.

gaps.construction: Clitic climbing barred with hay que, parecer, verbs of saying/believing (hay que hacerlo, *lo hay que hacer; creen saberlo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Shifting the clitic where climbing is barred — with hay que, parecer, or verbs of saying/believing — producing \"*lo hay que hacer\" or \"*lo creen saber\""
gaps.note: The page presents the periphrastic shift as generally available and never says it is barred with hay que, parecer or verbs of saying/believing, so a learner would produce the errors listed.

gaps.construction: Pronoun placement in periphrasis with gerund (Estoy leyéndolo / Lo estoy leyendo) and multiple clitics (Te lo estoy diciendo / Estoy diciéndotelo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "(Lo voy a comprar / Voy a comprarlo; Te lo estoy diciendo / Estoy diciéndotelo)"
gaps.note: The page shifts only with ir a + infinitive and querer, and does not show the gerund-periphrasis shift or the indirect+direct pronoun combination.

gaps.construction: Neuter lo with predicates (Parece cansado, pero no lo está)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "neuter lo for ideas/predicates"; constructionVariants: "replacing a whole idea, clause or predicate rather than a noun (... Parece cansado, pero no lo está)"
gaps.note: The page covers neuter lo only for clauses, not for replacing an adjective or noun predicate with ser/estar/parecer.

gaps.construction: Estar in preterite and future with gerund (Estuve hablando dos horas; Mañana a estas horas estaremos volando)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Estar in other tenses frames a bounded stretch (Estuve hablando dos horas) or progress at a future moment (Mañana a estas horas estaremos volando).
gaps.note: The page only teaches present and imperfect estar (table and uses); an exercise requiring preterite (estuve/estuvo...) or future (estaré/estaremos...) forms, or the bounded-duration and future-moment uses, has no support.

gaps.construction: Preterite estar + gerund with attached/preposed pronoun (Lo estuve buscando un buen rato)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: Lo estuve buscando un buen rato.
gaps.note: The page never shows estar in the preterite (estuve, estuviste...) or the 'for a while' bounded meaning, so this example type can't be worked out.

gaps.construction: Estar + siendo (Estás siendo muy amable hoy)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: Estás siendo muy amable hoy.
gaps.note: The irregular gerund of ser (siendo) and the use of estar + siendo for temporary behavior are never presented.

gaps.construction: Verbs that reject the continuous (ir/venir/poder, states, posture: *estoy yendo, *está llevando corbata, *está sentándose)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Using the continuous where Spanish rejects it — with ir/venir/poder, for states, or for posture — producing "*estoy yendo", "*está llevando corbata", or "*está sentándose"
gaps.note: The pitfalls section never warns about verbs/contexts where the continuous is not used; the page even lists venir → viniendo and poder → pudiendo as gerunds without noting restrictions.

gaps.construction: ¡Qué + noun + tan/más + adjective! (¡Qué día tan bonito!; ¡Qué película más aburrida!)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: ¡Qué + noun + tan/más + adjective! (¡Qué día tan bonito!)
gaps.note: The page never presents this as a pattern: it has no table row, no explanation of tan/más, and no example in the formation or examples sections. ¡Qué día tan bonito! appears only in the pitfalls, and más never appears. An exercise would ask the learner to build ¡Qué + noun + tan/más + adjective!.

gaps.construction: Dropping tan/más between noun and adjective (*¡qué día bonito!)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Dropping tan/más between the noun and its adjective ("*¡qué día bonito!" instead of "¡qué día tan bonito!" or "¡qué día más bonito!").
gaps.note: The pitfalls section never says tan/más is required between a noun and its adjective. An exercise on error correction could test this.

gaps.construction: Impersonal hacer in other tenses (Hacía mucho frío) and weather noun with hoy (Hoy hace sol)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: impersonal hacer + a weather noun, with no subject (Hace calor; Hacía mucho frío; Hoy hace sol)
gaps.note: The page shows only the present tense of hacer. It never shows the imperfect hacía, so a learner has no model for it.

gaps.construction: estar a + temperature in other tenses (Mañana estaremos a treinta)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: estamos a + a number + grados for the temperature (Estamos a quince grados; Mañana estaremos a treinta)
gaps.note: Only the present estamos is shown. The future estaremos is not.

gaps.construction: ¡Qué + noun! with weather/abstract nouns (¡Qué suerte!; ¡Qué calor!) and ¡Qué + adjective! alone (¡Qué interesante!)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: an exclamative ¡Qué + noun! with NO article (¡Qué vida!; ¡Qué suerte!; ¡Qué calor!)
gaps.note: The page gives only ¡Qué vida! as a bare-noun example. It does not show ¡Qué calor! linking exclamatives to weather.

gaps.construction: Other fixed exhortatives (¡Que te mejores!; ¡Que aproveche!) formation
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: a fixed exhortative with que + subjunctive, wishing something on someone (¡Que aproveche!; ¡Que te mejores!; ¡Que tengas buen viaje!)
gaps.note: The page shows the present subjunctive only as a label and gives only tengas as a model. It does not explain how to form it, for example for mejorarse.

gaps.construction: Resultar + adjective in dative frame (Me resulta difícil madrugar)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Resultar and ser + adjective follow the same pattern (me resulta difícil, le es útil).
gaps.note: The page never mentions resultar and gives no example or rule; an exercise on 'Me resulta difícil madrugar' (including agreement/conjugation of resultar) has no support.

gaps.construction: Ser + adjective in dative frame (Le es muy útil ese diccionario)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [resultar-ser-adjective, share 2] resultar or ser + adjective in the same dative frame (Me resulta difícil madrugar; Le es muy útil ese diccionario)
gaps.note: The page does not teach ser (es/son) + adjective with a clitic, nor the adjective use, so a learner can't produce 'le es útil'.

gaps.construction: Molestar as a gustar-type verb (Me molestan los ruidos)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: gustar-plain-clitic-frame ... a gustar-type verb (gustar, encantar, doler, interesar, molestar)
gaps.note: Molestar appears in the variant list but is never named on the page, though the general rule would let a learner generalize.

gaps.construction: desde hace + period with negative present-tense verb (No la veo desde hace dos años)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [desde-hace-duration, share 2] ... (Trabajo aquí desde hace seis meses; No la veo desde hace dos años)
gaps.note: The page only mentions desde hace in a bullet and one example with an affirmative verb; it never shows a formation rule/table for it or the negative-present use (No la veo desde hace dos años) that an exercise could test.

gaps.construction: Pronominal imperative of estar (estate quieto, estense tranquilos)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "the pronominal imperative of estar (estate quieto, estense tranquilos)"
gaps.note: The page never mentions estar or its pronominal imperative (estate + adjective/adverb, estense for ustedes), so an exercise on this variant could not be solved.

gaps.construction: Courtesy imperfect (Buenos días, quería un kilo de tomates; ¿Podía usted repetirlo?)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "the courtesy imperfect for polite requests (Quería hablar con el director)"
gaps.note: The page never mentions the courtesy/politeness use of the imperfect with querer, poder, or desear, yet an exercise would ask the learner to soften a request with quería/podía.

gaps.construction: algunos/algunas de + definite noun phrase (Algunos de los estudiantes no entendieron)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [algunos-de-phrase] algunos/algunas de + a definite noun phrase, the only quantifier Spanish allows there — never *unos de los
gaps.note: The page never mentions algunos de + definite NP or that unos cannot be used there; an exercise would demand algunos de los alumnos.

gaps.construction: Adverbial nada 'not at all' (No me gusta nada; No estoy nada cansado)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: adverbial nada = "not at all" (No me gusta nada) ... extend the set
gaps.note: The page treats nada only as a pronoun 'nothing'; it does not teach nada as an adverb modifying a verb or adjective after no.

gaps.construction: ni siquiera 'not even' (Ni siquiera me llamó)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [ni-siquiera] ni siquiera meaning 'not even', placed before the verb or the element it emphasises, needing no additional no
gaps.note: The page never introduces ni siquiera, its meaning, or that it takes no extra no.

gaps.construction: en mi vida as pre-verbal negative expression (En mi vida he visto algo así)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: 'one placed before the verb drops it (Nunca voy, Nadie vino), as does en mi vida (En mi vida lo he visto)'
gaps.note: The page only covers single negative words before the verb; the negative expression en mi vida and its no-dropping is never taught.

gaps.construction: Using unos before de instead of algunos
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Using unos before de, producing "*unos de los alumnos" instead of "algunos de los alumnos"
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address this error.

gaps.construction: No queda ningún billete / no … ningún + noun with pre-verbal ningún
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [algun-ningun-apocopation] ... No queda ningún billete
gaps.note: Apocopation is covered, but the table is confusing and algún in affirmative questions has little explanation; coverage is mostly adequate.

gaps.construction: Full clitic order se > te/os > me/nos > lo/la/los/las, with me/te/nos/os in the cluster (Se te ha caído la tinta; Se nos olvidó el nombre; Se me perdieron las llaves)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: clitics follow the fixed order se > te/os > me/nos > lo/la/los/las (Se te ha caído la tinta).
gaps.note: The page only gives the order for le→se + lo/la/los/las. It never teaches se + me/te/nos/os (se me cayó, se nos olvidó) or the rule that se always comes first, so an exercise on clustering would have no explained basis.

gaps.construction: Dative of possession with me/te/nos (Se me perdieron las llaves; Se te ha caído la tinta)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: dative-of-possession ... (Se le rompió el brazo a Carlos; Se me perdieron las llaves; Le robaron la cartera)
gaps.note: The page only shows the dative of possession with le, never with me/te/nos. Exercises will demand se me / se te / se nos with accidental-event verbs (perderse, olvidarse, romperse).

gaps.construction: Pitfall: me/te placed before se (*me se cayó el vaso)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Putting me/te before se, producing "*me se cayó el vaso" instead of "se me cayó el vaso" — se always comes first in a clitic cluster.
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address the *me se error.

gaps.construction: Plural le/les doubling and plural-number coverage (Les expliqué el problema a mis padres; Les expliqué la situación)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: clitic doubling: le/les together with an explicit a + named indirect object (Les expliqué el problema a mis padres)
gaps.note: Plural les is in the paradigm, but all doubling examples and the lone le/les case are singular. The page has no example of les with an a-phrase or of le/les alone with no a-phrase or DO clitic.

gaps.construction: Le/les alone as whole indirect object (Le escribí ayer)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [io-pronoun-le-les] le or les alone as the whole indirect object — no direct-object clitic, no a-phrase (Les expliqué la situación; Le escribí ayer)
gaps.note: The page explains le/les in general but gives no example of the bare pronoun with no a-phrase and no DO clitic.

gaps.construction: Invariable adjective-adverbs with set verbs (hablar claro, comprar barato, respirar hondo, trabajar duro; Habla más alto)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [adjective-adverb-set-verbs] an invariable adjective used adverbially with its set verb (hablar claro, comprar barato, respirar hondo, trabajar duro) — no -mente here
gaps.note: The page never mentions adjectives used directly as adverbs after set verbs (no -mente), so an exercise on hablar claro / comprar barato / Habla más alto gives the learner no rule.

gaps.construction: Viewpoint/sentence -mente adverbs (Personalmente, lo dudo; Económicamente, el país va mal)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "and viewpoint -mente (Económicamente, el país va mal)"
gaps.note: The page only covers manner and degree uses; it never explains -mente adverbs as sentence-initial viewpoint/stance adverbs set off by a comma.

gaps.construction: Adjectives that reject -mente (ordinals, nationalities) and alternatives (en segundo lugar, a la argentina)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Attaching -mente to adjectives that reject it (ordinals, nationalities, physical appearance), producing \"*segundamente\" or \"*argentinamente\" instead of \"en segundo lugar\" or \"a la argentina\"."
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address adjectives that cannot take -mente or the periphrastic alternatives.

gaps.construction: Avoiding stacked -mente adverbs; recast with con + noun (con una rapidez increíble)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Modifying one -mente adverb with another (\"*increíblemente rápidamente\") instead of recasting with con + noun (\"con una rapidez increíble\")."
gaps.note: The page even models a -mente adverb modifying an adjective but never warns against one -mente adverb modifying another or offers the con + noun alternative.
