gaps.construction: Coordination drop with contrastive conjunction and non-final adverbs (Actuó rápida pero cuidadosamente)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [mente-coordination-drop] ... (Habló lenta y claramente; Actuó rápida pero cuidadosamente)
gaps.note: The page says 'a conjunction' generally but only shows 'y' and does not show three-or-more series or 'pero'.

gaps.construction: recién + past participle (recién pintado, recién casados, una casa recién construida)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [recien-participle, share undefined] recién + past participle for something newly done, agreeing with the noun (recién pintado, recién casados, una casa recién construida)
gaps.note: The page never mentions recién + participle, its meaning, or its agreement with the noun, so a learner could not do an exercise like 'el banco está recién pintado'.

gaps.construction: comenzar a + infinitive as a variant of empezar a
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: empezar a (or comenzar a) + infinitive for the start of an action
gaps.note: The page only covers empezar a and never mentions that comenzar a works the same way.

gaps.construction: Periphrases in past tenses and progressive (Empecé a trabajar, Solíamos ir, Está empezando a llover, No vuelvas a hacerlo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: empezar a ... (Empecé a trabajar en marzo; Está empezando a llover); volver a ... (Volví a leer el libro; No vuelvas a hacerlo); soler ... (Solíamos ir a la playa)
gaps.note: The page only tabulates present-tense auxiliary forms; imperfect soler forms, preterite use, the progressive and negative imperative are never shown or explained.

gaps.construction: Obligatory a before alguien, nadie, quién (No veo a nadie; ¿A quién llamaste?)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "but obligatory before alguien, nadie, and quién (No veo a nadie)"
gaps.note: The page never mentions alguien/nadie/quién or that a stays despite non-specificity; an exercise like 'No veo __ nadie' or '¿__ quién llamaste?' cannot be solved from the page.

gaps.construction: querer/tener sense shift (querer a un hijo = love; querer un hijo = want one)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "With querer/tener, a shifts the sense: querer a un hijo = love him, querer un hijo = want one."
gaps.note: The page never discusses querer or tener or how presence/absence of a changes meaning; exercises would demand choosing between 'Quiere a su hijo' and 'Quieren tener un hijo'.

gaps.construction: Place names take no a (Visité Madrid) vs. collective nouns read as people take a (Admiro al pueblo cubano)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "no a before a place name after visitar, abandonar, ver (Visité Madrid en abril), but a before a collective noun read as people (Admiro al pueblo cubano)"
gaps.note: The page only says non-human objects omit a; it never addresses place names with visitar/abandonar or collective nouns, nor the error '*visité a Madrid'.

gaps.construction: Interrogative ¿A quién...? / comparative 'como a una reina'
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: "Me trataba como a una reina."
gaps.note: The example with a before an indefinite 'una reina' in a comparison is not explained; the page says a is omitted before indefinite-article persons.

gaps.construction: Specific person with indefinite article takes a (Busco a un médico que conozco) / specific vs. non-specific distinction with 'que hable inglés'
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "Busco un médico que hable inglés; La empresa necesita un fontanero"
gaps.note: The page only briefly notes the specific-indefinite exception as 'advanced'; subjunctive-relative contexts are not shown.

gaps.construction: adquirir i→ie (adquiero, adquieres, adquieren)

gaps.construction: aislar hiatus accent (aíslo, aíslas)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants boot-hiatus-accent: "aislar (aíslo)"

gaps.construction: caber yo-form contrasted with regular other persons (quepo / cabes)

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants orthographic-yo-ger-gir-guir: "elegir → elijo and corregir → corrijo, which also change e→i"

gaps.construction: sonreír: sonrió / sonrieron
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "(pidió/pidieron, durmió/durmieron, sintió, siguió, eligió, sonrió)"
gaps.note: The page never mentions sonreír, an -eír verb whose third-person form (sonrió, sonrieron) does not fit the -ir e→i or vowel-stem y rules it states, so an exercise on it would have no support.

gaps.construction: estar and tener U-stem preterites (estuve, tuve)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [u-stem-preterite] ... andar (anduve), estar (estuve), tener (tuve)
gaps.note: The core list and tables never include estar (estuv-) or tener (tuv-), so a learner cannot work out estuve or tuve, which exercises on this variant will likely test.

gaps.construction: hacer and its compounds (hice/hizo → deshizo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [compound-strong-preterite] ... chosen from compounds of poner, hacer, venir, tener or decir — e.g. ... deshacer (deshizo)
gaps.note: The page never gives hacer's stem (hic-/hiz-, with the c→z change in the él form), so a learner cannot produce deshizo or similar compounds of hacer.

gaps.construction: Compounds of tener, venir and decir (detuvieron, contuvo, previno, predijo, supuse)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [compound-strong-preterite] ... suponer (supuse), prevenir (previno), detener (detuvieron), contener (contuvo), predecir (predijo)

gaps.construction: -guar verbs with dieresis: averiguar → averigüé
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Rare -guar verbs also take a dieresis: averiguar → averigüé.
gaps.note: The page never mentions -guar verbs or the gu → gü dieresis change, yet examplesPositive includes "Averigüé su dirección anoche" and an exercise could ask for averigüé.

gaps.construction: Adverb placement outside haber + participle (Siempre he dicho lo mismo; Lo he repetido muchas veces)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [adverb-outside-haber-participle] an adverb placed OUTSIDE the haber + participle unit, which nothing may split — before haber or after the participle (Siempre he dicho lo mismo; Lo he repetido muchas veces)
gaps.note: The page only says 'nothing comes between them' and never shows an adverb before haber or after the participle, nor warns against '*he siempre dicho'; an exercise placing adverbs would not be solvable.

gaps.construction: Clitic pronoun placement with the perfect (La he visto hace un momento; Sí, las he probado; habértelo dicho)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: La he visto hace un momento.

gaps.construction: Just-now/same-day events with the perfect; hace un momento; esta mañana, este año (Esta mañana me he levantado a las seis)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: the perfect anchored by a present-oriented marker — ya, todavía no, hoy, esta mañana, este año (Esta mañana me he levantado a las seis)

gaps.construction: Irregular participles dicho, puesto, vuelto, abierto, roto, muerto
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: the irregular participles hecho, escrito, visto, dicho, puesto, vuelto, abierto, roto, and muerto
gaps.note: Dicho, puesto, vuelto, abierto and roto are only listed by name in a sentence, and muerto (morir) is never mentioned, though exercises will test all nine.

gaps.construction: Pitfalls on regularized forms *ponido, *rompido, *volvido
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "*hacido" for "hecho", "*escribido" for "escrito", "*rompido" for "roto", "*ponido" for "puesto", "*volvido" for "vuelto".
gaps.note: Pitfalls address only hacer, escribir, ver; the other irregular verbs' regularization errors are not covered.

gaps.construction: Short answers keeping the participle (—¿Has probado las fresas? —Sí, las he probado / Sí)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Deleting the participle in a short answer on the English model, producing "—¿Has probado las fresas? —*Sí, he"
gaps.note: The page never addresses answering questions with the perfect or that the participle cannot be dropped.

gaps.construction: Benefactive reflexive 'get done for oneself' (Me voy a cortar el pelo; Se está arreglando las uñas)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "and "get done for oneself" (me voy a cortar el pelo)."
gaps.note: The page never explains that the reflexive can express having something done for oneself by someone else; an exercise on cortarse el pelo / arreglarse las uñas would have no support.

gaps.construction: Reflexive marking intransitive change of state (casarse, dormirse: Mi hermana se casó; El niño se durmió enseguida)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "Also marks intransitives (casarse, dormirse)"
gaps.note: The page covers only actions done to oneself and inherent reflexives; it never teaches the reflexive as marking change of state with verbs like casarse or dormirse.

gaps.construction: Inherently pronominal verbs with prepositions (atreverse a, arrepentirse de, darse cuenta de, quejarse de)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "quejarse, atreverse a, arrepentirse de, darse cuenta de (Siempre se queja del trabajo; ¿Te atreves a hablar en público?)"

gaps.construction: Dropping se from an inherently pronominal verb (*quejo de todo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Dropping se from an inherently pronominal verb, producing "*quejo de todo" or "*atrevo a hacerlo""
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address omitting the pronoun with inherently pronominal verbs.

gaps.construction: Reflexive with periphrastic future / progressive (Me voy a cortar el pelo; Está vistiéndose / Se está arreglando)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "Está vistiéndose ahora mismo"; "Se está arreglando las uñas"
gaps.note: The page mentions the pronoun can go before or attach with an infinitive after a conjugated verb, but does not show the same option with estar + gerund (se está / está vistiéndose) or the written accent on gerund forms.

gaps.construction: si + present perfect for by-then completion (Si no ha cambiado para el viernes, avísame)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [si-perfect-apodosis-imperative] si + present PERFECT for something to be completed by a given point, usually with an imperative (Si no ha cambiado para el viernes, avísame)
gaps.note: The page says the protasis always uses si + present indicative and never shows or explains the present perfect (haber + participle) after si, yet exercises will test it.

gaps.construction: si + past indicative for fulfilled/habitual conditions (Si teníamos dinero, íbamos al teatro)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [si-past-indicative-habitual] si + a PAST indicative for a fulfilled or habitual condition, with a past main clause (Si teníamos dinero, íbamos al teatro)
gaps.note: The page never mentions past indicative (imperfect) in the si clause with a past main clause; it says the protasis always uses the present, so a learner could not solve such exercises.

gaps.construction: Contrast of sí/si in context, including emphatic sí and choosing between them (Sí, claro que voy / Si vienes, avísame)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: the spelling contrast between si ("if") and sí ("yes"/emphatic)
gaps.note: The page covers sí = yes and mentions emphasis only in passing, with no emphatic-use example and no side-by-side exercise-style contrast of choosing the right form.

gaps.construction: antes (bare, 'beforehand') and antes que + pronoun (Lola se levantó antes que nadie; Llegué antes que tú)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "bare antes \"before(hand)\" with antes que + pronoun (Lola se levantó antes que nadie), distinct from the formal preposition ante"
gaps.note: The page never mentions bare antes or antes que + pronoun (nor the contrast with ante), so a learner could not complete an exercise like 'Llegué ___ tú'.

gaps.construction: desde que + clause (Vivo aquí desde que nací)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "desde/desde que/desde hace for duration since a point or over a length of time"
gaps.note: desde que is named in the intro but never explained, tabulated or exemplified, so learners can't produce 'desde que + conjugated verb'.

gaps.construction: desde + clock time/event point (Está esperando desde las ocho)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "desde + a calendar or clock POINT ... (Está esperando desde las ocho)"
gaps.note: The page mentions year, date or event but gives only a year example, with no clock-time example.

gaps.construction: varios/varias 'several' (Compré varios libros; en varias partes del país)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [varios-agreement-no-article, share 2] varios/varias meaning 'several', agreeing with the noun and standing before it with no article
gaps.note: The page never mentions varios/varias (title, table, rules, examples and pitfalls all omit it), yet exercises will test its meaning, agreement and lack of an article.

gaps.construction: demasiado as adverb modifying a verb (Hablas demasiado)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [demasiado-adverb-invariable, share 2] demasiado as an invariable ADVERB modifying an adjective or a verb, where it must not agree (Este ejercicio es demasiado difícil; Hablas demasiado rápido)
gaps.note: The page says the adverb modifies an adjective or another adverb and never mentions modifying a verb (Hablas demasiado, Trabajan demasiado).

gaps.construction: nada/nadie before the verb (Nadie vino; Nada me gusta)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [nada-nadie-negative-pronouns] nada or nadie as a negative pronoun, before the verb or after it with no
gaps.note: The page states the rule for preverbal nada/nadie but gives no example of them before the verb, only postverbal examples.

gaps.construction: Reflexive third-person sí / consigo with mismo (Está disgustado consigo mismo; Los estudiantes hablan entre sí)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: reflexive third person uses sí (mismo) and consigo (hablan entre sí, disgustado consigo mismo), though speech often prefers él/ella.
gaps.note: The page only glosses sí in a table note and gives one consigo example; it never explains that sí/consigo refer back to the subject, how mismo/misma is added, entre sí, or that él/ella is often preferred in speech, so a learner couldn't produce the exercise sentences.

gaps.construction: Prepositional a + tonic pronoun instead of a clitic with verbs of motion (se acercó a ella, not *se le acercó)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Using a clitic with verbs of motion instead of preposition + tonic pronoun, producing "*se le acercó" instead of "se acercó a ella".
gaps.note: The pitfalls section never addresses using preposition + tonic pronoun rather than a clitic after verbs of motion such as acercarse.

gaps.construction: quedarse/acabar + gerundio (Me quedé ayudándolos hasta tarde; Acabó cediendo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [quedarse-acabar-gerundio] quedarse or acabar + gerundio for how something ended up (Me quedé ayudándolos hasta tarde; Acabó cediendo)
gaps.note: The page never mentions quedarse/acabar + gerundio, so a learner could not form or interpret sentences like 'Acabarás haciendo lo que ella diga'.

gaps.construction: resultative tener + agreeing participle (Ya tengo compradas las entradas)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [tener-participle-agreement] resultative tener + a past participle AGREEING with the object (Ya tengo compradas las entradas; Tenemos hechos los deberes)
gaps.note: The page doesn't teach resultative tener + participle or that the participle agrees in gender and number with the object, and it even says the non-finite form never changes.

gaps.construction: Participle agreement error (*tengo comprado las entradas)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Leaving the participle invariable in resultative tener + participle ("*tengo comprado las entradas" instead of "tengo compradas las entradas").
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address participle agreement with tener.

gaps.construction: estar para + infinitivo (Está para llover)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: estar a punto de + infinitivo (to be about to; also estar para + infinitivo)
gaps.note: The page gives only estar a punto de and never mentions the alternative estar para + infinitivo.

gaps.construction: continuar + gerundio (Continúa lloviendo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [seguir-gerundio] seguir (or continuar) + gerundio for an action still going on (Sigo estudiando alemán; Continúa lloviendo)
gaps.note: Continuar as a synonym of seguir with the gerund is not mentioned.

gaps.construction: Negative imperative with dejar de (No dejes de llamarme)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [dejar-de-infinitivo] dejar de + infinitive for stopping an action (Dejé de fumar hace un año; No dejes de llamarme)
gaps.note: The page doesn't show negated dejar de, which means 'keep doing' (No dejes de llamarme), so a learner could misread the meaning.

gaps.construction: Partitive with first-person pronoun: la mayoría de nosotros creemos
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: partitive-de-plural-agreement: "la mayoría de nosotros"
gaps.note: The page only shows third-person plural verbs after collective + de + noun, so it never shows that 'de nosotros' gives a first-person plural verb (creemos), which an exercise could demand.

gaps.construction: Participle as predicate with a singular collective: Toda la clase quedó sorprendida
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: collective-predicate-adjective-singular: "PREDICATE ADJECTIVE or participle must also be singular ... Toda la clase quedó sorprendida con la noticia"
gaps.note: The page covers only predicate adjectives (la gente está cansada). It never mentions participles or verbs like quedar, and it never shows a 'toda la + collective' subject.

gaps.construction: Partitive collectives beyond 'mayoría': un grupo de turistas esperaban, la mitad de los socios
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: partitive-de-plural-agreement: "un grupo de estudiantes, la mitad de los socios ... Un grupo de turistas esperaban en la puerta"
gaps.note: The table shows only 'la mayoría de'. Other partitives (un grupo de, la mitad de) and de + bare plural noun without an article appear only in passing or not at all.

gaps.construction: Modest/softened opinions: Yo diría que...
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "modest opinions (yo diría que...)"
gaps.note: The page never presents softening an opinion as a use of the conditional (diría appears only in the stem table), yet an exercise would ask the learner to produce "yo diría que..." or similar.

gaps.construction: Advice with deberías + infinitive (Deberías consultar a un especialista)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "advice (deberías + infinitive)"
gaps.note: Advice is mentioned in passing under polite requests/suggestions, but deber in the conditional and its pairing with an infinitive are never shown or exemplified.

gaps.construction: Softening a request with conditional instead of present/future (¿Podrías ayudarme? vs ¿Puedes ayudarme?)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Using the present or future tense instead of the conditional to soften a request (e.g. \"¿Puedes ayudarme?\" instead of \"¿Podrías ayudarme?\")."
gaps.note: The page says the conditional is more courteous than the present, but the pitfalls section does not address this error; it only covers the future-vs-conditional error in si-clauses.

gaps.construction: Epistemic poder/podría + infinitive for speculation (No contesta; podría estar durmiendo todavía / Podría ser tu tía)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [poder-epistemic-probability] epistemic poder/podría + infinitive for speculation about what may be the case (No contesta; podría estar durmiendo todavía)
gaps.note: The page never mentions poder as a way to speculate, so a learner could not do an exercise that asks for podría/puede + infinitive to express conjecture.

gaps.construction: Modal + haber + participle for past reference, including poder (Deben de haber salido ya; Podría haber salido)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [modal-haber-participle-past] a modal — deber, deber de, poder — + haber + participle for PAST reference (Debería haberlo hecho la semana pasada; Deben de haber salido ya)
gaps.note: The page has only one note with two examples. It does not explain the meaning contrast (regret or unfulfilled obligation with debería haber, past conjecture with deber de haber) and never shows poder + haber.

gaps.construction: Clitic pronoun placement with modal + haber + participle (Lo debería haber hecho vs. Debería haberlo hecho)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: modal + haber + participle covers past reference (Debería haberlo hecho / Lo debería haber hecho)
gaps.note: The page shows only the attached-clitic order and says nothing comes between deber and the infinitive. It never presents the alternative order with the pronoun before the modal.

gaps.construction: Additive connectors además / es más (Es caro; además, es feo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Also additive además / es más
gaps.note: The page never mentions además or es más; an exercise requiring an additive connector would have nothing to rely on.

gaps.construction: Dismissive de todas formas / de todos modos (De todas formas, llámame mañana)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: De todas formas, llámame mañana.
gaps.note: The page has no explanation or example of de todas formas / de todos modos, although it appears in examplesPositive.

gaps.construction: Emphatic en realidad / de hecho
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: emphatic en realidad / de hecho with explanatory es que + clause
gaps.note: The page never teaches en realidad or de hecho, so an exercise on them could not be solved.

gaps.construction: Explanatory es que + clause (¿Por qué no viniste? — Es que no dormí en casa)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: ¿Por qué no viniste? — Es que no dormí en casa.
gaps.note: The page never mentions es que as an excuse or explanation reply, though it is in the examples and description.

gaps.construction: Contrastive en cambio / por otra parte, and no obstante as a sin embargo substitute
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: Other adverbial connectors of the same shape may stand in: no obstante, en cambio, por otra parte
gaps.note: The page covers only sin embargo as an adversative. An exercise may use en cambio, por otra parte or no obstante, and the page doesn't teach them or how they differ.

gaps.construction: Sin embargo in other positions (joining two clauses within one sentence, or mid-clause)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: adversative sin embargo joining two clauses, or opening the second sentence
gaps.note: The page only shows sin embargo at the start of Clause B after a semicolon or full stop, and says it always starts Clause B. It does not show it joining two clauses in one sentence.

gaps.construction: Future of probability with verbs other than ser, e.g. estar + gerund (No contesta, estará durmiendo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [futuro-probabilidad, share 2] the EPISTEMIC future — a guess about the PRESENT ... (¿Qué hora es? — Serán las once; No contesta, estará durmiendo)
gaps.note: The page defines the probability future and gives only the single example Serán las once. It never shows it with other verbs or with estar + gerund, so an exercise on a present-time guess like 'estará durmiendo' relies on the learner generalising.

gaps.construction: uno/una + 3sg generic (Uno nunca sabe qué puede pasar; una for female speakers)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Related generics: uno/una + 3sg verb (Uno nunca sabe; una for female speakers)
gaps.note: The page never mentions uno/una as a generic, its 3sg verb, or the gender choice; an exercise on the uno-generic variant or the example 'Uno nunca sabe qué puede pasar' could not be solved from it.

gaps.construction: Informal impersonal tú (Si lo piensas, es increíble)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [impersonal-tu] informal impersonal tú addressing people in general, not the listener (Si lo piensas, es increíble)
gaps.note: The page never teaches the 2sg verb with generic meaning, so a learner could not produce or recognise impersonal tú.

gaps.construction: Register contrast: uno/se preferred in formal register
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: uno/se preferred in formal register
gaps.note: The page gives no guidance on register or on choosing between the impersonal plural, uno, se and impersonal tú.

gaps.construction: hacía + period + que + imperfect (Hacía años que no la veía)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [hacia-period-que-imperfect] the past-shifted hacía + a period + que + imperfect (Hacía años que no la veía; Hacía meses que no salíamos)
gaps.note: The page never presents hacía ... que + imperfect, though exercises will require it; learners get no formation or example.

gaps.construction: tardar + en + infinitive (Tardamos tres horas en montar el armario)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [tardar-en-infinitive] tardar + en + infinitive for how long something takes (Tardé dos horas en llegar)
gaps.note: The page does not mention tardar at all; an exercise would require the learner to use tardar + en + infinitive for how long something takes.

gaps.construction: dentro de + period (Vuelvo dentro de dos semanas)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [dentro-de-period] dentro de + a period for a point measured forward from now (El tren sale dentro de diez minutos)
gaps.note: The page never covers dentro de for time measured forward from now.

gaps.construction: Completed duration: past tense + (durante) + period (Trabajé durante años en Madrid)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [past-tense-durante-period] a COMPLETED duration: a past tense + (durante) + a period (Vivimos allí tres meses)
gaps.note: The page only covers ongoing durations and never teaches that finished durations use a past tense with (durante) + period, contrasted with llevar/hace que.

gaps.construction: hace + period + que + preterite meaning 'ago' (hace un año que lo vi)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: hace ... que + preterite is correct but means "ago" (hace un año que lo vi)
gaps.note: The pitfall mentions the preterite changes meaning but frames it only as an error. It doesn't teach 'ago' as a valid use, though the example gives the gist.

gaps.construction: hacía ... que tense pairing (hacía + imperfect)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Mixing the tense pairs: ... hacía ... que the imperfect (hacía años que no la veía)
gaps.note: The pitfalls section addresses only hace ... que + present vs. preterite and never the hacía + imperfect pairing.

gaps.construction: Negative ongoing duration with hace...que no / llevar sin (Hace una semana que no llueve)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [hace-period-que-present] (Hace una semana que no llueve)
gaps.note: The page shows only a negative with llevar (No llevo mucho tiempo estudiando) and no example of hace ... que + negated present, i.e. a state of not doing something.

gaps.construction: Adjective nominalization with determiner (los viejos, una rota, uno parecido)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [adjective-nominalizer, share 2] a determiner + ADJECTIVE standing for a full noun phrase, with masculine un becoming uno (Los viejos ya no funcionan; Tengo una rota; Busco uno parecido)
gaps.note: The page never teaches that adjectives can nominalize with a determiner (article/indefinite), nor that masculine un becomes uno (uno parecido); it even says Spanish never inserts uno, and exercises on this variant would be unsolvable.

gaps.construction: Indefinite uno/una + adjective (prefiero uno parecido pero más barato)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: No quiero este bolso; prefiero uno parecido pero más barato.
gaps.note: This positive example with indefinite uno is not shown or explained anywhere on the page; the page only warns against uno.

gaps.construction: Impersonal se with human object taking le/les (Se le nota cansada; Se les ve contentos)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [impersonal-se-human-object] impersonal se acting on a specific HUMAN object, which takes le/les (Se le nota cansada; Se les ve contentos)
gaps.note: The page only shows 'se busca a los culpables' with personal a and never teaches the le/les pronoun with se (Se le/les + verb + adjective), so a learner couldn't produce 'Se les ve contentos'.

gaps.construction: uno/una + pronominal verb (Uno se levanta temprano; Una se cansa de repetirlo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [uno-with-pronominal-verb] uno/una + an already pronominal verb, since two ses cannot co-occur (Uno se levanta temprano)
gaps.note: The page never mentions uno/una as a substitute for impersonal se with reflexive/pronominal verbs, nor the ban on two ses; exercises would require this.

gaps.construction: Avoiding doubled se (*se se levanta temprano)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Doubling se to make a pronominal verb impersonal ("*se se levanta temprano" instead of "uno se levanta temprano")
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address the doubled-se error or its fix with uno.

gaps.construction: Passive se with modal + infinitive, verb agreeing with plural noun (Se tienen que resolver varios problemas)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: Se tienen que resolver varios problemas.
gaps.note: The page never shows agreement when se is followed by a modal/periphrastic verb plus infinitive (the conjugated verb agrees with the plural noun), which an exercise would demand.

gaps.construction: Ojalá (que) + present subjunctive (Ojalá que encuentres trabajo pronto)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [subj-with-ojala] an independent wish introduced by ojalá (que) + present subjunctive (Ojalá que encuentres trabajo pronto; Ojalá haga sol mañana)
gaps.note: The page never mentions ojalá or independent wishes, yet exercises will require producing ojalá + subjunctive.

gaps.construction: Quizá / quizás / tal vez + present subjunctive (Quizá venga mañana)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [subj-with-quiza-tal-vez] quizá, quizás or tal vez followed by the present subjunctive to mark real uncertainty (Quizá venga mañana; Tal vez no sepan la respuesta)
gaps.note: The page does not cover adverbs of uncertainty as subjunctive triggers; an exercise would demand quizá/tal vez + subjunctive.

gaps.construction: A lo mejor + indicative (A lo mejor llueve)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [indicative-after-a-lo-mejor] a lo mejor + the INDICATIVE, never the subjunctive — the exception that contrasts with quizá/tal vez (A lo mejor llueve esta tarde)
gaps.note: The page never states that a lo mejor takes the indicative, so learners can't solve this exercise type or avoid the *a lo mejor llueva error.

gaps.construction: Noun + de que + subjunctive (la esperanza de que llueva)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [noun-de-que-subj] an abstract noun + de que + present subjunctive (la esperanza de que llueva; el miedo de que se enteren; la posibilidad de que cierren)
gaps.note: The page only covers verb and impersonal triggers; noun + de que is never taught.

gaps.construction: Fronted el hecho de que / el que + subjunctive (El hecho de que no haya venido me molesta)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [fronted-el-hecho-de-que-subj] a fronted el hecho de que (or bare el que) clause in the subjunctive, placed before the main clause (El que digas eso me sorprende)
gaps.note: No mention of subject clauses fronted with el hecho de que / el que.

gaps.construction: Independent que-wishes and third-person commands (¡Que te vaya bien!; Que entren)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [que-wish-command] an independent que-clause used as a wish or third-person command, with no main verb (¡Que te vaya bien!; Que entren de uno en uno; Que descanses)
gaps.note: The page only treats subjunctive in dependent clauses with a main verb; que + subjunctive without a main verb is never shown.

gaps.construction: Temer que / me temo que and quejarse de que taking the indicative
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Using the subjunctive after quejarse de que or after me temo que meaning "I'm afraid (= regret to say)", which take the indicative ("*me temo que sea tarde" instead of "me temo que es tarde").
gaps.note: The page lists temer que as a subjunctive trigger and never mentions the indicative exception with me temo que or quejarse de que.

gaps.construction: estar preterite vs. imperfect: estuvo (state finally reached after hasta que / una vez que) vs. estaba (No descansó hasta que estuvo delante de mí)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [estar-pret-vs-imperf, share undefined] estar: estuvo = a state finally reached, typical after hasta que / una vez que, vs. estaba = was, ongoing
gaps.note: The page lists only conocer, saber, poder, querer, tener; estar, estuvo/estaba and the trigger phrases hasta que / una vez que are never taught, yet an exercise would test them (including the fourth positive example).

gaps.construction: a quien for human direct objects (el chico a quien saludaste)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "a quien for human objects: el chico a quien saludaste"
gaps.note: The page only shows quien after prepositions like con; it never explains personal 'a' + quien for human direct objects, which an exercise would require.

gaps.construction: Proper names and tonic pronouns reject restrictive relatives (*Juan que vive aquí)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "the restriction that proper names and tonic pronouns reject restrictive relatives"
gaps.note: The page never states that proper names/tonic pronouns can't take restrictive relatives (need commas/non-restrictive), nor lists it as a pitfall.

gaps.construction: Noun + que + infinitive (tengo cosas que hacer; necesito algo para comer)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "noun + que + infinitive (tengo cosas que hacer; but necesito algo para comer)"
gaps.note: The page does not teach relative que with an infinitive or the contrast with 'para + infinitive' after algo/nada.

gaps.construction: Verb–Subject order keeping que next to its antecedent (es el perro que compró mi amigo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "Verb–Subject order keeping que next to its antecedent (es el perro que compró mi amigo)"
gaps.note: The page gives no explanation of postposed subjects or keeping the relative clause adjacent to its antecedent.

gaps.construction: No quien(es) in restrictive clauses without a preposition (*los hombres quienes dijeron eso)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Using \"quien(es)\" in a restrictive clause without a preceding preposition"
gaps.note: The table hints quien is used after prepositions, but the page never states that quien is wrong in a plain restrictive clause with no preposition, and even says non-restrictive quien is fine; the pitfalls section does not address it.

gaps.construction: Avoiding English-style gerund modifiers (*una chica hablando francés)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Using a gerund to modify a noun, English-style (\"*una chica hablando francés\" instead of \"una chica que habla francés\")"
gaps.note: The page does not warn that a relative clause with que, not a gerund, must modify a noun.

gaps.construction: Restrictive donde with expressed antecedent in varied contexts (Volvimos al café donde nos conocimos)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: "Volvimos al café donde nos conocimos hace diez años."
gaps.note: Donde is covered, but there is no mention that it requires an expressed antecedent or the contrast with en que/en el que.

gaps.construction: Perfect reporting verb keeps the present (Juan ha dicho que viene; Ha dicho que está en casa)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [perfect-report-present-retained] a PERFECT reporting verb (ha dicho / ha comentado / ha avisado), which counts as a present tense, so the reported present is KEPT and not shifted
gaps.note: The page never says the present perfect counts as a present-zone reporting verb, and it has no example or table row with ha dicho que viene, so a learner can't work out that no shift happens.

gaps.construction: Over-applying backshift after the perfect (*ha dicho que venía)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Over-applying the shift to a present-zone reporting verb, backshifting after the perfect ("*ha dicho que venía" instead of "ha dicho que viene" when he is still on his way).
gaps.note: The pitfalls section doesn't cover this error, and an exercise could test it directly.

gaps.construction: Shift is kept after a past verb even when the fact is still true
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: after a past one Spanish normally shifts even when the statement still holds
gaps.note: The page presents the present-reporting case as 'still-relevant fact' but never says that Spanish backshifts after a past verb even when the fact is still true, unlike English.

gaps.construction: Present-zone reporting verbs other than decir (pide, dicen) and past reporting verbs (contó, comentó, aseguró, dijeron)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: a past-tense reporting verb (dijo/dijeron/contó/comentó/aseguró)... a present-zone reporting verb (dice/dicen/pide/ha dicho)
gaps.note: The page only uses decir (plus pensar/creer in passing) and never shows contar, comentar, asegurar or pedir as reporting verbs, including pedir for requests.

gaps.construction: estar con + noun for ailment or accompaniment (Está con tos; Estoy con mis padres)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: estar con + noun for a current ailment or accompaniment (Está con tos); constructionVariants: [estar-con-ailment-accompaniment, share 2]
gaps.note: The page says it covers four patterns and never explains or exemplifies estar con + noun for illness or being with someone, so a learner could not do exercises on it (e.g., Está con gripe, Estoy con mis padres).

gaps.construction: parecer + adjective vs. parece que, contrasted as different structures (Parece cansado vs. Parece que está cansado)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: parecer + adjective agreeing with its subject, or impersonal parece que + indicative — the two being different structures
gaps.note: The page gives a rule and one example of each, but it never shows agreement with a plural or feminine subject (parecen cansados) and never contrasts the two structures directly.

gaps.construction: ser for day/date of an event (La boda es el sábado)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [ser-event-time, share 3] ser for WHEN an event takes place — clock time, day or date (El examen es a las diez; La boda es el sábado)
gaps.note: The page only demonstrates clock time (a las diez); it never shows day or date phrases (el sábado, el 5 de mayo) with ser, which an exercise on this variant could require.

gaps.construction: sin que + subjunctive (Salió sin que nadie lo viera)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "and sin que + subjunctive for "without (someone) doing" (Salió sin que nadie lo viera)"
gaps.note: The page never mentions sin que (not in intro, rules, examples or pitfalls), yet exercises will test it with a different-subject subjunctive clause.

gaps.construction: sin + infinitive when subjects match (salí sin despedirme)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "same-subject sentences take sin + infinitive"; commonErrors: "using \"sin que\" at all when the subjects match, where \"sin\" + infinitive is required (salí sin despedirme)"
gaps.note: No explanation of the same-subject restriction or the sin + infinitive alternative; an exercise would demand choosing between sin que and sin + infinitive.

gaps.construction: Indicative after sin que error (*sin que nadie lo vio)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Using the indicative after \"sin que\" (\"*sin que nadie lo vio\")"
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address indicative after sin que.

gaps.construction: antes de que with past reference (Terminó antes de que llegáramos)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: "antes de que + subjunctive, which takes the subjunctive whatever the time reference (Llámame antes de que salgas; Terminó antes de que llegáramos)"
gaps.note: The page says it always takes subjunctive but frames it as future-only and never shows past-tense context or the imperfect subjunctive form (llegáramos), which an exercise may require.

gaps.construction: Elative -ísimo on adverbs: -mente adverbs (clarísimamente, rapidísimamente) and lejos/cerca → lejísimos/cerquísima
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [elative-isimo-adverb] the elative on an ADVERB: -ísima- infixed inside a -mente adverb (clarísimamente, rapidísimamente) or an irregular form such as lejísimos or cerquísima (Vive lejísimos del centro)
gaps.note: The page treats -ísimo only on adjectives and never mentions adverbs, the -ísima- infix in -mente adverbs, or lejísimos/cerquísima, so an exercise like 'Vive ___ del centro' cannot be solved.

gaps.construction: jugar a + article, contraction al (jugar al ajedrez, jugar al fútbol)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [jugar-a-article-contraction] jugar a + the definite article before a game or sport, contracted to al in the masculine singular
gaps.note: The page never mentions jugar a, the article before games, or the a + el → al contraction, yet an exercise would demand 'jugábamos al ajedrez'.

gaps.construction: Adjective + preposition (amable con, harto de, capaz de, contento con)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [adj-prep-regime] the fixed prepositional regime of an ADJECTIVE (amable con, harto de, capaz de, responsable de, contento con)
gaps.note: The page only treats verbs; an exercise would ask for 'amable con' or 'harto de', which the page never teaches.

gaps.construction: Noun + preposition (miedo a, amor por/hacia, ganas de, interés en)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [noun-prep-regime] the fixed prepositional regime of a NOUN (miedo a, amor por/hacia, ganas de, interés en)
gaps.note: No noun regime is presented; learners could not produce 'Le tiene miedo a la oscuridad' or 'amor por los animales'.

gaps.construction: Preposition retained before que-clause (me di cuenta de que…; queísmo/dequeísmo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [prep-retained-before-que] the governed preposition retained before a que-clause ... Never insert a spurious de after a verb of saying (dice que, not *dice de que)
gaps.note: The page never covers keeping the preposition before que (darse cuenta de que, estar seguro de que) or avoiding dequeísmo with decir que; exercises would test this.

gaps.construction: Infinitive, never gerund, after a preposition (Estoy harto de esperar; Se negó a firmar)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [prep-infinitive-not-gerund] an INFINITIVE (never a gerund) as the complement of a governed preposition
gaps.note: The page lists infinitive complements in passing but never states the rule that the infinitive, not the gerund, follows a preposition, nor addresses the gerund error (*harto de diciéndotelo).

gaps.construction: Other regime verbs: depender de, casarse con, saber/oler a, contar con, negarse a, ayudar a
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: depender de, jugar a + article, casarse con, saber/oler a, negarse a, ayudar a
gaps.note: Only hablar, pensar, soñar, invitar are taught (depender de is merely mentioned in a pitfall); exercises would use casarse con, saber a (Esta sopa sabe a ajo), negarse a, contar con.

gaps.construction: Prenominal-only adjectives: mero, pleno, supuesto, llamado, tamaño, sendos (un mero malentendido; en pleno invierno; el supuesto culpable)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [prenominal-only-adjectives, share 2] an adjective that only works BEFORE the noun — mero, pleno, supuesto, llamado, tamaño, sendos
gaps.note: The page never mentions adjectives that can only go before the noun, so a learner could not solve exercises like 'un mero trámite' or 'en pleno invierno' or avoid '*un trámite mero'.

gaps.construction: Relational adjectives always postnominal (una política energética; un virus informático; la reforma educativa)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [relational-adjectives-postnominal, share 2] a relational, classifying adjective that must stay AFTER the noun because it names a category rather than a quality
gaps.note: The page says nothing about relational or classifying adjectives that must stay postnominal. It also doesn't say they can't take más/menos or be used predicatively, so exercises on 'política energética' or 'virus informático' have no support.

gaps.construction: Example 'El gobierno presentó su nueva política energética' (nueva before a noun alongside a relational adjective)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: El gobierno presentó su nueva política energética.
gaps.note: The page doesn't show how a prenominal nuevo combines with a postnominal relational adjective. The page also glosses prenominal nuevo as 'another, a different', which does not fit this example.

gaps.construction: Treating relational adjectives like ordinary ones (not gradable with más/menos, rarely predicative: la vida familiar)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Treating relational adjectives (virus informático, política energética, la vida familiar) like ordinary ones — they are always postnominal, not gradable with más/menos, and rarely predicative.
gaps.note: The pitfalls section doesn't address this error.

gaps.construction: Postposing prenominal-only adjectives error (*un trámite mero)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Postposing the prenominal-only adjectives mero, pleno, supuesto, llamado, tamaño, sendos ("*un trámite mero" instead of "un mero trámite")
gaps.note: The pitfalls section doesn't cover this error.

gaps.construction: Colloquial que linking an imperative/warning to its reason (¡Date prisa, que se va el tren!; Ponte el abrigo, que hace frío)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [colloquial-que, share 2] colloquial que attaching a reason to an imperative or a warning (¡Date prisa, que se va el tren!; Ponte el abrigo, que hace frío)
gaps.note: The page never mentions colloquial 'que' after an imperative or warning (not in the intro, table, examples or pitfalls), yet exercises would require producing or recognizing it.

gaps.construction: First/second-person focus agreement (El que llamó fui yo; Somos nosotros quienes decidimos)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants cleft-person-quien: "if the focus is a first- or second-person pronoun, ser and the relative verb agree with it (Fue Juan quien llamó anoche; El que llamó fui yo; Somos nosotros quienes decidimos)"
gaps.note: The page only shows third-person foci and never explains that ser and the relative verb agree with a yo/tú/nosotros/vosotros focus, which an exercise would require.

gaps.construction: Relative-clause verb agreement with plural 1st/2nd person focus (vosotros fuisteis los que lo visteis; tú fuiste el que lo vio)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Using third-person agreement in the relative clause when the focus is a plural first or second person ("*vosotros fuisteis los que lo vieron" instead of "los que lo visteis") — third person is only accepted in the singular"
gaps.note: The page never says the relative verb must be first/second-person plural (and may be third-person only in the singular), so the pitfall cannot be solved.

gaps.construction: Subject-initial el que cleft with ser + focus after (El que manda aquí soy yo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: "El que manda aquí soy yo."
gaps.note: The page teaches only ser + focus + relator order; it never shows the reversed pseudo-cleft with el que/la que/los que as subject and the person focus after ser.

gaps.construction: Ser agreeing with a plural or personal predicate (todo son problemas; el jefe eres tú)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Making ser agree with the singular or neuter subject instead of a plural or personal predicate ("*todo es problemas" instead of "todo son problemas"; "*el jefe es tú" instead of "el jefe eres tú")"
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address ser agreeing with the focus rather than the subject, which an exercise could test.

gaps.construction: ello after prepositions (No hablemos de ello; Por ello decidí quedarme)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [ello-after-preposition] neuter ello as the complement of a preposition, referring to a whole idea (No hablemos de ello; Por ello decidí quedarme)
gaps.note: The page says it covers three patterns and never mentions neuter ello; an exercise requiring ello after a preposition could not be solved from the page.

gaps.construction: le with creer, pegar, obedecer or an inanimate subject (No le creo a Juan; Le espera una catástrofe)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [le-with-specific-verbs-inanimate-subject] le for a human object with creer, pegar or obedecer, or where the subject is inanimate (No le creo a Juan; Le espera una catástrofe)
gaps.note: The page never teaches le with creer/pegar/obedecer or with inanimate subjects, though the examplesPositive include 'Le espera una catástrofe'. An exercise would demand le in these cases.

gaps.construction: Fronted object with a personal 'a' (A tu hermana la vi ayer) and fronted human objects
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [fronted-object-doubling] ... (Los libros los tiene Juan; A tu hermana la vi ayer)
gaps.note: All page examples are inanimate objects. The page never shows a fronted human object with personal 'a' plus the clitic.

gaps.construction: Contrastive 'a ella / a él' after a clitic (La vi a ella, pero no a él)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: La vi a ella, pero no a él.
gaps.note: The page does not show clitic doubling with a stressed prepositional pronoun for contrast.

gaps.construction: Doubling clitic with todo as direct object (lo sé todo; me lo tienes que contar todo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Dropping the doubling clitic when todo is the direct object ("*sé todo" instead of "lo sé todo")
gaps.note: The page only gives fronted 'Todo lo sé'. It does not cover postverbal todo, where the clitic is also required, and its pitfalls section does not address this.

gaps.construction: Fronted bare object takes no clitic (*dinero no lo tengo)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Adding a resumptive clitic to a fronted bare object with no determiner ("*dinero no lo tengo" instead of "dinero no tengo")
gaps.note: The page states the rule once (Carne no como) in 'when to use'. Its pitfalls section does not warn against adding the clitic.

gaps.construction: Neuter lo with plural or adjective-predicate questions (¿Son caros? — No lo son)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [neuter-lo-predicate-echo] ... (¿Estás cansada? — Lo estoy; ¿Son caros? — No lo son)
gaps.note: The page shows only affirmative replies. It never shows a negated reply with no preceding lo.

gaps.construction: mucho/poco agreeing before más/menos/mayor/menor + noun (muchas más oportunidades, muchos menos hijos, mucha mayor velocidad)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Leaving mucho/poco invariable before más/menos/mayor/menor + noun ("*mucho más casas" instead of "muchas más casas") — they agree in gender and number
gaps.note: The page never says that mucho/poco agree in gender and number with the noun when they intensify más/menos + noun, so a learner could not complete an exercise like "Ahora hay ___ más oportunidades que antes".

gaps.construction: Future perfect for anteriority to another future event, e.g. Cuando lleguemos ya se habrá ido (cuando + subjunctive clause, with ya)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "actions completed before a future reference point (Cuando lleguemos ya se habrá ido)"
gaps.note: The page only shows a deadline use (Para mañana habré llegado) and never shows a future reference point given by a second clause, such as cuando + subjunctive, so an exercise combining the two clauses has no model.

gaps.construction: Contrast with simple future where anteriority is needed (*cuando lleguemos, ya se irá vs. ya se habrá ido)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Using the simple future where anteriority to another future event is required (e.g. \"*cuando lleguemos, ya se irá\" instead of \"ya se habrá ido\")."
gaps.note: The pitfalls section covers only ser/estar and participle agreement, and never warns against using the simple future in place of the future perfect.

gaps.construction: Future perfect for probability about the recent past in declarative sentences (Habrá tenido problemas; Ya habrá llegado a casa a estas horas)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "probability about the recent past (Habrá tenido problemas)"
gaps.note: The page gives only a vague 'conjecture about past events' and one question example (¿Habrán salido ya?). It has no declarative example and does not explain that this means 'probably has/have done'.

gaps.construction: Conditional como + subjunctive for threats/warnings (¡Como vuelvas a llegar tarde, te quedas sin salir!), vs causal como + indicative
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [como-conditional-subjunctive, share 2] conditional como + SUBJUNCTIVE in a threat or warning, distinct from causal como + indicative (¡Como vuelvas a llegar tarde, te quedas sin salir!)
gaps.note: The page never mentions conditional como, its threat/warning use, or the contrast with causal como + indicative, so a learner could not do an exercise on it.

gaps.construction: De + infinitive as a same-subject if-clause (De haberlo sabido, no habría venido)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [de-infinitive-if-clause, share 2] de + INFINITIVE as a same-subject if-clause, usually with a conditional main clause (De haberlo sabido, no habría venido)
gaps.note: The page has no mention of de + infinitive (simple or compound) as a conditional clause, how it is formed, or its pairing with a conditional main clause.

gaps.construction: Pluperfect subjunctive conjugation in the si-clause (si hubieras sabido, si hubiéramos llegado, si hubieran venido)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: habría + participle as the result of a si + pluperfect subjunctive counterfactual (Si me lo hubieras dicho, te habría ayudado)
gaps.note: The page only mentions 'hubiera/hubiese + participle' in the pitfalls and never gives the imperfect subjunctive forms of haber for each person, so an exercise needing the si-clause with 2sg, 1pl or 3pl subjects gives the learner no paradigm.

gaps.construction: suficiente(s)/bastante/demasiado (como) para + infinitive (Ha vendido suficientes coches como para ganarse el viaje)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [enough-or-too-para-infinitive] suficiente(s)/bastante/demasiado + (como) para + infinitive for "enough/too … to"
gaps.note: The page never mentions the 'enough/too … to' construction with para + infinitive (or como para), so a learner has no way to do exercises on it.

gaps.construction: de quien / del que / de la que as spoken alternative to cuyo (un autor del que conozco las novelas)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [de-quien-del-que-spoken-alternative, share 2] the spoken alternative to cuyo — de quien / del que / de la que — in a sentence where written Spanish would use cuyo
gaps.note: The page lists the forms and gives one example in a closing note. It never explains that del/de la/de los/de las que agrees with the antecedent, or that the possessed noun then takes its own article (las novelas), unlike cuyo. An exercise asking learners to rewrite a cuyo sentence with de quien or del que would have little support.

gaps.construction: como + gerund = como si (Me miró como calculando mi edad)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [como-gerund-como-si, share 2] como + gerund for a manner that resembles a hypothetical action, the compact equivalent of como si + subjunctive (Me miró como calculando mi edad; Movía las manos como buscando algo)

gaps.construction: Predicative adjective agreeing with the subject (Sonrió tranquila; Ellas viven felices aquí)

gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: superlative time expressions with neuter lo (lo antes posible).

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [le-dative-infinitive-own-object] the dative le/les with a perception verb whose infinitive carries its OWN direct object (Juan le oyó cantar un aria; Les vimos preparar la cena)

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [medio-invariable-adverb] adverbial medio before an adjective, invariable however the subject agrees — distinct from adjectival media hora (Están medio dormidas; La puerta quedó medio abierta)

gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Using próximo for narrative "next" ("*el próximo día" in a past narrative instead of "al día siguiente") — próximo / que viene count from now, siguiente from the narrative anchor.

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [middle-se-person-experiencer] the pronominal form of a psych verb, with a PERSON as subject undergoing the state (Se preocupa por todo; Se enamoró de ella en un mes)

gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: se me olvidó, se me ocurrió, se me acabó

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [no-dudar-que-indicative] no dudar que + INDICATIVE, the exception where negation does NOT trigger the subjunctive (No dudo que es verdad; No niego que tiene talento)

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: a negated verb of saying — decir, contar, mencionar — in a past tense ... (No me dijo que hubiera venido a la fiesta; Nadie mencionó que estuviera enfermo)
gaps.note: The page only treats decir; contar, mencionar and negative subjects like nadie are not shown, though the general rule could be extended.

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: no creo que + present subjunctive (No creo que Marta tenga razón; No creemos que sea buena idea)

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: reduplicative-subjunctive — verb + lo que + same verb, verb + donde/como + same verb, or verb + o no (Pase lo que pase, seguiremos adelante; ...)
gaps.note: The page never mentions or explains the reduplicative structure (verb + lo que/donde/como + same verb, or verb + o no), so an exercise asking learners to complete or produce 'Digan lo que digan' or 'Le guste o no' has no support.

gaps.construction: Factual concessives y eso que / si bien with indicative only (No la reconocí, y eso que la había visto muchas veces)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: factual-concessive-indicative-only — a FACTUAL concessive — y eso que, si bien — which takes the indicative only, y eso que following the main clause

gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Extending the subjunctive to the factual concessives "y eso que" and "si bien", which take only the indicative
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address this error.

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: Mientras estudiaba, escuchaba música; description: después (de) que, mientras, una vez que
gaps.note: The page gives only apenas as an indicative past example. It has no habitual imperfect example and no worked example for después de que, una vez que or mientras. The general rule does cover these.

gaps.construction: Aunque + subjunctive for a hypothetical future concession (Aunque llueva, saldremos); a pesar de que

gaps.note: The page covers only the 'unknown to speaker' use of aunque. It gives no future/hypothetical example like 'Aunque llueva', and no example with a pesar de que.

gaps.construction: plain quedar (non-reflexive) for lasting states, slightly more formal (quedó ciego)

gaps.note: The page only presents reflexive quedarse and says nothing about non-reflexive quedar as a more formal alternative, which exercises could require.

gaps.construction: Ablative of material (tahtadan bir masa; altından bir yüzük)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [ablative-material, share 1] ablative -DAn marking the MATERIAL something is made of (tahtadan bir masa; altından bir yüzük)

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [fixed-case-verbs-ablative, share 2] a verb that GOVERNS the ablative... kork-, hoşlan-, nefret et-, bık-

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [fixed-case-verbs-dative, share 2] a verb that GOVERNS the dative... inan-, güven-, bin-, yardım et-, başla-
gaps.note: The page covers only goal and recipient datives and never teaches verb-governed dative, so exercises on inan-/güven-/bin- have no support.

gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Calquing English transitives with the accusative on fixed-case verbs (*köpeği korkuyorum, *seni inanıyorum ...)
gaps.note: The pitfalls section does not address using the accusative instead of the required ablative/dative with these verbs.

gaps.note: Only 'Bir şey aldım' is shown; hiçbir şey and bare mass nouns like çay are not illustrated.

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [bare-np-completed-duration, share 1] a COMPLETED duration or a distance as a bare noun phrase with neither -DIr nor -DEn beri, predicate in the definite past (Dün iki saat bekledim; Beş kilometre yürüdük)

gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [degil-contrastive-constituent, share 1] değil negating a SINGLE CONSTITUENT contrastively, "not X but Y" (Elma değil, armut yiyorum; Bugün değil, yarın)

gaps.construction: Posture verbs: event vs. state (oturdu "sat down" vs oturuyordu "was sitting")

gaps.construction: Partitive frame: dergilerin hepsi, paranın yarısı, öğrencilerin çoğu
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [genitive-possessive-partitive, share 1] the partitive frame: a plural or mass noun in the genitive + a quantity word carrying the 3sg possessive (dergilerin hepsi; paranın yarısı; öğrencilerin çoğu)
gaps.note: The page never mentions partitives or quantity words (hepsi, yarısı, çoğu) taking -(s)I after a genitive plural/mass noun, so an exercise on this variant has no support.

gaps.construction: Plural possessor with singular possessed (çocukların öğretmeni) vs. plural possessed (çocukların öğretmenleri)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: çocukların öğretmeni (the children's teacher — a plural possessor still takes 3sg -(s)I when one thing is possessed; çocukların öğretmenleri usually means "the children's teachers")
gaps.note: The page covers no plural possessors (genitive -ların after plural -lar) and does not explain that the possessed still takes 3sg -(s)I, or how a plural possessed is marked.

gaps.construction: Negative possession with yok (Ahmet'in arabası yok) and full-noun possessor in var/yok
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: genitive possessor (or a pronoun) + possessed noun carrying the 3sg possessive + var/yok (Onun bir kedisi var; Ahmet'in arabası yok)
gaps.note: The page only shows a pronoun possessor with var; it never shows yok or a noun/proper-name possessor in a var/yok sentence.

gaps.construction: Pronoun genitive forms (onun, and others)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: genitive possessor (or a pronoun) + possessed noun carrying the 3sg possessive + var/yok
gaps.note: Only onun appears (in an example); the page gives no pronoun genitive forms, though exercises may use pronoun possessors.

gaps.construction: Warning adverb sakın with negative imperative (Sakın unutma! / Sakın geç kalmayın!)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [imperative-sakin-warning, share 1] the warning adverb sakın, which REQUIRES a negative -mA imperative in the same clause (Sakın unutma!; Sakın geç kalmayın!) — never with a bare positive stem
gaps.note: The page never mentions sakın, so a learner cannot handle an exercise that adds sakın to a negative imperative or must reject it with a positive stem.

gaps.construction: Determiner placement with a -ki phrase (öbür gazetedeki resim vs. gazetedeki öbür resim)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Placing a determiner before the -ki phrase when it should modify the head noun: öbür gazetedeki resim = "the picture in the OTHER paper"; for "the other picture in the paper" the determiner follows: gazetedeki öbür resim.
gaps.note: The pitfalls section never covers where a determiner goes relative to the -ki phrase, so an exercise on word order of determiner, -ki phrase and head noun has no support.

gaps.construction: -ki on a genitive noun phrase (not only pronouns), e.g. Ali'nin → Ali'ninki
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Relativiser -ki turns a locative/genitive/time phrase into a modifier
gaps.note: The page shows genitive -ki only on the pronoun benim, so an exercise using a genitive noun (Ali'ninki) would have no example to generalise from.

gaps.construction: Locative phrase modifying an indefinite noun (age/size/style): dört yaşında bir çocuk
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: dört yaşında bir çocuk (a four-year-old child — a locative phrase can modify an indefinite noun, typically for age/size/style)
gaps.note: The page only covers static location and never shows the locative in an age/attributive phrase (with possessive -ında), so a learner couldn't build or interpret this.

gaps.construction: Quantified frequency with locative on time unit: haftada iki kez, ayda bir
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: haftada iki kez (twice a week — quantified frequency puts the locative on the time unit: ayda bir = once a month)
gaps.note: The page never teaches the distributive/frequency use of -DA on time units, so an exercise on 'x per week/month' has no basis.

gaps.construction: Plural stems with locative (-lAr + DA): çocuklarda, evlerde
gaps.curriculumEvidence: coverageSpec: number: singular, plural
gaps.note: Exercises will test plural nouns with the locative, but the page shows no plural noun taking -DA (plural -lAr then -da/-de) and never states the ordering or harmony after -lar/-ler.

gaps.construction: Front-vowel voiceless stems also take -te (sepette)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Applying -ta/-te only to back-vowel stems and forgetting that front-vowel voiceless stems also soften (işte, sepette).
gaps.note: Only işte illustrates front-vowel voiceless assimilation; the pitfalls section doesn't address this error explicitly, though the general rule covers it.

gaps.construction: artık "no longer" with negative predicate (Artık evimiz yok; Artık burada oturmuyoruz)

gaps.note: The page never mentions artık or how it means "no longer" with negation; an exercise requiring artık + negative predicate cannot be solved from the page.

gaps.construction: daha / henüz "not yet" (Daha gelmediler; Henüz hazır değilim)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [negation-adverb-daha-henuz, share 1] daha / henüz "not yet" with a negative predicate
gaps.note: The page does not teach daha/henüz as "not yet" with negation, so exercises using them have no support.

gaps.construction: bir daha "(n)ever again" (Bir daha gelmem; Bir daha yapmayacağım)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [negation-adverb-bir-daha, share 1] bir daha "(n)ever again" with a negative predicate
gaps.note: The page never introduces bir daha with negation; an exercise would demand this sense and the page gives none.

gaps.construction: Negation with değil (Daha hazır değilim) / nominal predicate negation
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: daha/henüz = "not yet" (Daha hazır değilim)
gaps.note: Examples in the entry use değil with adjectives; the page only mentions değil in passing as an invalid verb form and never explains it.

gaps.construction: Negation with 2sg, 1pl, 2pl, 3pl person endings
gaps.curriculumEvidence: coverageSpec: person: 1sg, 2sg, 3sg, 1pl, 2pl, 3pl
gaps.note: The table shows only 1sg forms and no person-suffix paradigm for -yor and -DI (e.g. gelmiyorsun, gelmedik, gelmediler), though exercises will test all persons.

gaps.construction: Negation of the future (Bir daha yapmayacağım) and aorist (Bir daha gelmem)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: bir daha "(n)ever again" ... (Bir daha gelmem; Bir daha yapmayacağım)
gaps.note: Examples use negative aorist (gelmem) and future (yapmayacağım) forms, which the page never shows; it only treats present continuous and past.

gaps.construction: bir as indefinite article after adjective (genç bir adam, açık bir pencere) vs. numeral bir before adjective
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Defaulting to bir + adjective + noun order for a neutral indefinite (*bir genç adam): as the article, bir follows the adjective (genç bir adam, açık bir pencere); pre-adjective bir reads as the numeral "one".
gaps.note: The pitfalls section never addresses the bir-as-article word order (adjective + bir + noun), so an exercise on this error would have no support on the page.

gaps.construction: Dropping the subject pronoun in neutral statements (Geliyorum, not Ben geliyorum; no "O" across sentences once the referent is clear)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Overusing overt subject pronouns English-style: person marking on the predicate already identifies the subject, so neutral statements drop the pronoun (Geliyorum, not Ben geliyorum) — also across sentences once the referent is clear
gaps.note: The page says only that the subject pronoun is "often omitted; include it for emphasis or clarity". It gives no example of pro-drop, doesn't mention carrying the referent across sentences, and the pitfalls section skips this error, so a learner couldn't judge a drill on when to drop or keep the pronoun.

gaps.construction: Personal suffix on a pronoun as predicate: Kim o? — Benim!
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: Kim o? — Benim!
gaps.note: The page only attaches suffixes to nouns and adjectives. It never shows the suffix on a pronoun (ben → benim) or the answer to a 'Kim o?' question, so a learner couldn't produce or recognize this.

gaps.construction: Singular predicate with quantified subjects (Birçok kişi çocukluğunu düşünmez, not *düşünmezler)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "These quantified subjects keep the predicate singular too: Birçok kişi çocukluğunu düşünmez, not *düşünmezler."
gaps.note: The page never says that the verb stays singular after a numeral or quantifier subject, so an exercise on predicate agreement (e.g. choosing düşünmez vs *düşünmezler) has no support.

gaps.construction: her + singular noun (her gün, her öğrenci)
