gaps.note: The page lists only birkaç, çok and az as quantifiers and never mentions her, so a her + singular noun item rests on a vague 'most quantifiers' rule.

gaps.construction: birçok + singular noun (Birçok kişi)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "quantifiers like çok/her/birkaç ... Birçok kişi çocukluğunu düşünmez"
gaps.note: Birçok appears in the curriculum's own example but not on the page. Only çok and birkaç are named.

gaps.construction: Bare önce / sonra as discourse sequencers (Önce duş aldım, sonra kahvaltı ettim)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [bare-once-sonra-sequence, share 1] bare önce and sonra as discourse sequencers joining two clauses, with no complement attached (Önce duş aldım, sonra kahvaltı ettim)
gaps.note: The page covers only önce/sonra after a noun, pronoun or time span, and never teaches that bare önce/sonra at the start of a clause mean 'first' / 'then'. An exercise asking the learner to sequence two clauses would have nothing on the page to draw on.

gaps.construction: Negative present continuous: gelmiyorum, okumuyorsun, başlamıyor
gaps.curriculumEvidence: coverageSpec: polarity: affirmative, negative
gaps.note: The page only shows affirmative forms and never teaches the negative stem + -me/-ma + -yor (gelmiyorum, yapmıyoruz). Exercises with negative polarity would give the learner no way to form them.

gaps.construction: Yes/no questions with var/yok: var mı? (Evde süt var mı?; Telefonun var mı?)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: existential var / yok — "there is / there is not" in a place or situation (Evde süt var mı?; Burada kimse yok); possessive-var-yok (Telefonun var mı?)
gaps.note: The page never shows the question particle mı with var/yok (including its separate spelling and position after var), so a learner can't form or answer 'Evde süt var mı?'.

gaps.construction: Explicit possessor with genitive: Onun kedisi yok
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: possessive-var-yok ... (Arabam var; Telefonun var mı?; Onun kedisi yok)
gaps.note: The page only says the possessor is carried by the suffix with no separate pronoun, and never shows a noun/pronoun possessor in the genitive (onun, Ali'nin) before the possessed noun.

gaps.construction: Possessive suffix forms on consonant-final nouns (telefonun, kedisi, vaktim)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: possessive-var-yok — possessive suffix on the thing owned (Telefonun var mı?)
gaps.note: The suffix table only uses vowel-final araba; the page says suffixes follow vowel harmony but never gives the consonant-final variants (-im/-ın/-ı) that an exercise with telefon or kitap would need.

gaps.construction: Indefinite kimse with yok: Burada kimse yok
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: existential var / yok ... (Evde süt var mı?; Burada kimse yok)
gaps.note: The page never explains 'kimse' (nobody/anyone) with yok for existence of people.

gaps.construction: Locative -DA and ablative -DAn, including d/t assimilation (evde, işte, evden)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "2-way (e/a): plural -lAr, locative -DA, ablative -DAn."
gaps.note: The page only lists locative and ablative among case markers. It never gives the -da/-de/-ta/-te or -dan/-den/-tan/-ten forms or the voiceless-consonant d→t switch (işte). An exercise on the ablative or locative has nothing to work from.

gaps.construction: Dative -(y)A with buffer y (köprüye, eve, kapıya)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "dative -(y)A is 2-way (-(y)a/-(y)e)"
gaps.note: Dative is named as a case marker, but the page never shows its form, never says it follows the 2-way pattern, and never explains the buffer -y- after vowel-final stems. Dative is a coverageSpec value, so it will be drilled.

gaps.construction: Buffer consonant -y- in accusative -(y)I (kapıyı)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: "kapıyı (the door, accusative) — back unrounded /a/ stem → -ı"
gaps.note: The page shows only consonant-final accusatives (evi, okulu). It never explains inserting -y- after a vowel-final stem, so kapıyı cannot be produced.

gaps.construction: Past tense -DI harmonising in 4 ways (geldi, okudu)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "4-way (i/ı/u/ü): accusative -(y)I, possessive -(s)I, past -DI"
gaps.note: The page only lists "Verb conjugations" as a place harmony applies. It gives no past -DI example and no d/t alternation, so a past-tense harmony drill has nothing to work from.

gaps.construction: Which suffixes take 2-way vs 4-way harmony (plural, locative, ablative, dative = 2-way; accusative, possessive, past = 4-way)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Conflating the 2-way (low-vowel) and 4-way (high-vowel) harmony patterns — applying -lAr/-lEr logic to suffixes that take the 4-way pattern, such as the accusative -(y)I."
gaps.note: The page gives both tables but never says which suffix uses which pattern. The pitfalls section does not warn against mixing the patterns, and an exercise would require choosing the right pattern for each case.

gaps.construction: Possessive -(s)I with buffer -s- after vowel-final stems, and kitap→kitab- softening (kitabı, kapısı)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "possessive -(s)I"
gaps.note: Possessive appears only in table and example forms (kapısı, kitabı). The page never explains the -s- buffer or the p→b change, and it does not present possessive as a 4-way suffix to produce.

gaps.construction: Harmony follows the last vowel in ordinary loanwords (otobüs → otobüsler, kitap → kitaplar)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "Forgetting harmony follows the stem's last vowel even in loanwords (otobüs → otobüsler, kitap → kitaplar)"
gaps.note: The pitfalls section covers only exceptional loanwords with front suffixes after a back vowel. It does not say that regular loanwords still harmonise with their last vowel. The soft-l plural examples (meşguller, roller) are also missing, though the general soft-l point is covered.

gaps.construction: Forming the -mA + possessive verbal noun for lazım/gerek (gitmem lazım, gitmen lazım, gelmesi lazım)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [necessity-lazim-gerek] OBJECTIVE necessity by lexical means — lazım or gerek on a -mA/-mAk nominal (Eve gitmem lazım; Beklemek gerek)
gaps.note: The page only shows the single example 'gitmem lazım' and calls it a 'verbal noun'. It never explains that the noun is built from -mA plus a possessive ending, or how it changes across persons, so a learner could not produce 'gitmen lazım' or 'çalışmamız gerek'.

gaps.construction: gerek and the infinitive -mAk pattern (Beklemek gerek)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [necessity-lazim-gerek] ... lazım or gerek on a -mA/-mAk nominal (Eve gitmem lazım; Beklemek gerek)
gaps.note: 'gerek' is named once alongside lazım, but there is no example with gerek. The page also never shows the impersonal -mAk infinitive + gerek/lazım pattern that an exercise on 'Beklemek gerek' would require.

gaps.construction: Negative ability in the past tense and other tenses (Gelemedi, Görüşemedik)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [ability-negative-yama] the IRREGULAR negative ability -(y)AmA — never -Abilme (Yapamam; Gelemedi; Görüşemedik)
gaps.note: The negative tables and examples only use the aorist (yapamam, gelemem). The page never shows -(y)AmA combined with the past tense -DI (gelemedi, görüşemedik) or with other tenses.

gaps.construction: Bare adjectives as manner adverbs (güzel söyledi, zor yürüyor)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "Many simple adjectives also work bare as manner adverbs (güzel söyledi, zor yürüyor)"
gaps.note: The page never says that simple adjectives can function as manner adverbs without -CA, so a learner can't decide when to use bare adjective vs. -CA form in an exercise.

gaps.construction: bir şekilde / bir biçimde / olarak for derived or foreign adjectives (bilimsel olarak)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: "derived/foreign adjectives instead need bir şekilde/biçimde or olarak (bilimsel olarak)"
gaps.note: The page doesn't teach the alternative adverbial strategies for adjectives that don't take -CA (olarak is only mentioned for language names), so an exercise requiring 'bilimsel olarak' or 'X bir şekilde' has no support.

gaps.construction: madem / mademki shared premise (Madem yorgunsun, evde kal; Madem biliyordun neden söylemedin?)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: madem(ki) "since / seeing that" fronts a reason both speakers already know, with a question or suggestion following: Madem yorgunsun, evde kal.
gaps.note: The page never mentions madem/mademki, so a learner has no way to produce sentences with a fronted shared premise followed by a question or suggestion.

gaps.construction: dA after a numeral-modified noun phrase giving definite 'both/all' reading: (Her) iki çocuk da uyumuş
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: (Her) iki çocuk da uyumuş. (Both children had gone to sleep — dA after a numeral-modified noun phrase gives the definite "both/all" reading.)
gaps.note: The page never shows dA following a numeral + noun (iki çocuk da, hepimiz/her iki ... da) to mean 'both/all', so a learner could not do an exercise that requires this reading.

gaps.construction: Scalar bile in negative sentences, 'not even': Bir kuruş bile vermedi
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [bile-scalar-even] ... (Çocuklar bile biliyor; Bir kuruş bile vermedi)
gaps.note: The page only illustrates bile in an affirmative sentence and never shows it with a negative verb or a minimal-quantity NP (bir kuruş bile ... -medi) meaning 'not even'.

gaps.construction: Negation of a converb chain via the final verb (Onunla hiçbir zaman görüşüp konuşamadık, not *görüşmeyip)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: "the converb stays bare; only the final main verb is inflected for the whole chain, including negation: Onunla hiçbir zaman görüşüp konuşamadık ("we never managed to meet and talk"), not *görüşmeyip."
gaps.note: The page says only the final verb is inflected, but it never says that negation or ability goes on the final verb and not on the -(y)Ip converb. An exercise could ask the learner to negate a chain and the page doesn't show how.

gaps.construction: ister … ister with verbal imperative/optative halves, incl. negated second half (İster inan ister inanma)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [ister-ister] ister … ister, "whether … or", typically with imperative or optative halves (İster sen gel ister o; İster inan ister inanma)
gaps.note: The page shows only İster sen gel ister o and never explains that the halves are usually imperative/optative verbs or shows a verb/negated-verb pair like İster inan ister inanma, which an exercise could ask the learner to produce.

gaps.construction: Mass nouns reject numerals/kaç/birkaç (su, müzik); birkaç bira = bottles
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Mass nouns (su, müzik) reject numerals/kaç/birkaç unless a measure or type is meant (birkaç bira = bottles)

gaps.construction: biraz + mass noun (biraz su), not with count nouns
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: biraz takes mass nouns (biraz su), not count nouns.
gaps.note: The page does not mention biraz or its contrast with numerals/tane, yet an exercise could ask to choose biraz vs. numeral+tane.

gaps.construction: Ablative partitive with tane: Bunlardan iki tane alayım
gaps.curriculumEvidence: examplesPositive: Bunlardan iki tane alayım. (Let me take two of these — ablative partitive with a tane/measure head: şu elmadan bir kilo "a kilo of those apples".)
gaps.note: The page only shows tane before a noun; it never shows tane standing alone as the head of a phrase with an ablative 'of these' (bunlardan iki tane), or the measure-head variant (şu elmadan bir kilo).

gaps.construction: gibi gel- 'seem' idiom: Bana haklısın gibi geliyor
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: After a finite clause, gibi + gel- with a dative experiencer = "seem (to someone)": Bana haklısın gibi geliyor
gaps.note: The page never mentions gibi + gel- with a dative experiencer after a finite clause, so a learner could not produce or complete 'Bana ... gibi geliyor' sentences.

gaps.construction: -mIş gibi 'as if' clauses with optional sanki: (Sanki) hayalet görmüş gibi sapsarı oldu
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: after -mIş, gibi makes "as if" clauses, optionally with sanki: (Sanki) hayalet görmüş gibi sapsarı oldu.
gaps.note: The page treats gibi only after nouns/pronouns; it never shows gibi after a -mIş verb form or the particle sanki, which an exercise would demand.

gaps.construction: o kadar / öyle … ki result frame: O kadar yorgundum ki hemen uyudum
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [o-kadar-ki-result] the RESULT frame o kadar / öyle … ki, "so … that" ... (O kadar yorgundum ki hemen uyudum; Öyle güzeldi ki anlatamam)
gaps.note: The page never teaches the degree-intensifying o kadar/öyle with a ki-clause for result; an exercise on 'so ... that' would have no support.

gaps.note: The page only exemplifies approximate kadar with a time expression, with no example of a numeral with a counted noun (on beş kadar hasta) or the adverb use of equality kadar.

gaps.construction: Genitive on bu/şu/kim before gibi/kadar (bunun gibi, kimin kadar)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Forgetting that kadar — not only gibi — takes the genitive on ben/sen/biz/siz/bu/şu/o/kim

gaps.construction: Nested compounds keeping each head's -(s)I (İngiliz Edebiyatı Bölümü; göz hastalıkları hastanesi)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: Nested compounds keep each head's -(s)I (İngiliz Edebiyatı Bölümü)
gaps.note: The page never explains or shows a compound modifying another compound, so a learner cannot build or analyse göz hastalıkları hastanesi.

gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: a compound serving as head takes -(s)I only once (Polonya gölge tiyatrosu, not *tiyatrosusu)
gaps.note: The page does not say that -(s)I is not doubled when the head is itself a compound, so an exercise on this would have no support.

gaps.construction: Partitive with ablative-marked set + biri (arkadaşlarımdan biri, onlardan biri)

gaps.note: The page glosses biri as 'one of them' but never shows the ablative + biri frame, so a learner couldn't produce 'one of my friends'.

gaps.construction: asla 'never' obeys negative polarity (Asla özür dilemez, not *asla özür diler)

gaps.construction: ara and karşı paradigm forms (arasında/arasına/arasından, karşısında)

gaps.curriculumEvidence: coverageSpec: person: 1sg, 2sg, 3sg, 3pl

gaps.construction: 1st-person deliberative -sA question (Bu konuda kime danışsam acaba?; Ne yapsam?)

gaps.construction: Periphrastic -mIş olsaydI counterfactual (Üniversiteyi kazanmış olsaydı...)

gaps.construction: Negative forms of the compound pasts (gitmemişti, gitmezdi, gitmeyecekti, gitmemeliydi, gitmeseydi)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: coverageSpec: polarity: affirmative, negative
gaps.note: The page shows only affirmative forms. It never explains how to negate each base (-mA- before -mIş, -mAz- in the aorist, -mAyAcAk, -mAmAlI, -mAsA), so a learner could not do negative exercises.

gaps.construction: Aorist base -IrdI (okurdum) and the choice of aorist vowel
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [past-habitual-ardi] the copula on the AORIST base: -ArdI / -IrdI (Çocukken çok okurdum)
gaps.note: The page gives only the -ArdI type (giderdi, yapardı). It never mentions the -Ir- aorist allomorph or says when it is used, which an exercise with okurdum would need.

gaps.curriculumEvidence: description: (b) neutral generalization / definition in formal register (Türkiye'nin başkenti Ankara'dır; …kaynamaktadır)
gaps.note: The page never introduces the -mAktA + -DIr verb form (kaynamaktadır), which the description names as a formal generalization pattern, so a learner couldn't form or recognise it in a drill.

gaps.construction: -AsIyA adverb (e.g. ölesiye «to death, to the point of dying»)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: commonErrors: Over-producing the receding -AsI "worthy of" as if productive (yenilesi yemek) — living uses are frozen (kahrolası) or the -AsIyA adverb.
gaps.note: The page never mentions that the living remnant of -AsI is the adverbial -AsIyA, so a learner has no way to recognise or contrast it with the frozen adjectival -AsI.

gaps.construction: Reported necessity formation across persons: -mAsI gerektiğini (beklememiz gerektiğini belirtti; erken gitmeleri gerektiğini söyledi)
gaps.curriculumEvidence: constructionVariants: [reported-necessity-dik-accusative, share 2] ... -mAsI gerektiğini söyledi (Erken gitmem gerektiğini söyledi; beklememiz gerektiğini belirtti)
gaps.note: The page gives only one 1sg necessity example (gitmem gerektiğini) and its formation table covers only the -mA directive. It never shows how the possessive varies across persons in the necessity pattern (the bare -mA+possessive plus gerektiğini), and it never shows a matrix verb other than söylemek, such as belirtmek.
